_cl_disconnectreason.description: This cvar contains the reason for the last disconnection, so that mod menus can know why things failed.
_cl_disconnectreason.name: _cl_disconnectreason

_cl_voip_capturedevice_opts.description: The possible audio capture devices, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.
_cl_voip_capturedevice_opts.name: _cl_voip_capturedevice_opts

_pext_infoblobs.description: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Enables the use of very large infokeys containing potentially invalid chars. Note that the userinfo is still limited by sv_userinfo_bytelimit and sv_userinfo_keylimit.
_pext_infoblobs.name: _pext_infoblobs

_pext_lerptime.description: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Sends timing hints for interpolation.
_pext_lerptime.name: _pext_lerptime

_pext_vrinputs.description: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Networks player inputs slightly differently, allowing for greater capabilities, particuarly vr controller info.
_pext_vrinputs.name: _pext_vrinputs

_q3bsp_bihtraces.description: Uses runtime-generated bih collision culling for faster traces.
_q3bsp_bihtraces.name: _q3bsp_bihtraces

_s_device_opts.description: The possible audio output devices, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.
_s_device_opts.name: _s_device_opts

_vid_renderer_opts.description: The possible video renderer apis, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.
_vid_renderer_opts.name: _vid_renderer_opts

allow_download.description: If 1, permits downloading. Set to 0 to unconditionally block *ALL* downloads from this server. You may wish to set sv_dlURL if you wish clients to still be able to download content.
allow_download.name: allow_download

allow_download_configs.description: 1 allows downloading of config files, either with the extension .cfg or in the subdir configs/.\nTHIS IS DANGEROUS AS IT CAN ALLOW PEOPLE TO READ YOUR RCON PASSWORD ETC.
allow_download_configs.name: allow_download_configs

allow_download_copyrighted.description: 0 blocks download of packages that are considered copyrighted. Specifically, this means packages with a leading 'pak' prefix on the filename.\nIf you take your copyrights seriously, you should also set allow_download_pakmaps 0 and allow_download_pakcontents 0.
allow_download_copyrighted.name: allow_download_copyrighted

allow_download_demos.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the demos/ directory
allow_download_demos.name: allow_download_demos

allow_download_locs.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the locs/ directory
allow_download_locs.name: allow_download_locs

allow_download_logs.description: 1 permits downloading files with the extension .log\nTHIS IS DANGEROUS AS IT POTENTIALLY ALLOWS PEOPLE TO SEE PASSWORDS OR OTHER PRIVATE INFORMATION.\nNote that it can be switch on/off via rcon.
allow_download_logs.name: allow_download_logs

allow_download_maps.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the maps/ directory
allow_download_maps.name: allow_download_maps

allow_download_models.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the progs/ or models/ directory
allow_download_models.name: allow_download_models

allow_download_other.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file that was not covered by any of the directory download blocks.
allow_download_other.name: allow_download_other

allow_download_packages.description: if 1, permits downloading files (from root directory or elsewhere) with known package extensions (eg: pak+pk3). Packages with a name starting 'pak' are covered by allow_download_copyrighted as well.
allow_download_packages.name: allow_download_packages

allow_download_pakcontents.description: 0: clients may not download non-map files within the server's packages.\n1: clients may download such files so long as the package is not deemed copyrighted, for compat with old clients that do not support package downloads.\n2: client may download such files regardless of copyright state (WARNING! ONLY for consistency with vanilla QuakeWorld!).
allow_download_pakcontents.name: allow_download_pakcontents

allow_download_pakmaps.description: 0: clients may not download map files within the server's packages.\n1: clients may download such files so long as the package is not deemed copyrighted, for compat with old clients that do not support package downloads.\n2: client may download such files regardless of copyright state (WARNING! Should never be used!).
allow_download_pakmaps.name: allow_download_pakmaps

allow_download_particles.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the particles/ directory
allow_download_particles.name: allow_download_particles

allow_download_refpackages.description: If set to 1, packages that contain files needed during spawn functions will be become 'referenced' and automatically downloaded to clients.\nThis cvar should probably not be set if you have large packages that provide replacement pickup models on public servers.\nThe path command will show a '(ref)' tag next to packages which clients will automatically attempt to download.
allow_download_refpackages.name: allow_download_refpackages

allow_download_root.description: If set, enables downloading from the root of the gamedir (not the basedir). This setting has a lower priority than extension-based checks.
allow_download_root.name: allow_download_root

allow_download_skins.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the skins/ directory
allow_download_skins.name: allow_download_skins

allow_download_sounds.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the sound/ directory
allow_download_sounds.name: allow_download_sounds

allow_download_textures.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the textures/ directory
allow_download_textures.name: allow_download_textures

allow_download_wads.description: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the wads/ directory, or is in the root directory with the extension .wad
allow_download_wads.name: allow_download_wads

allow_skybox.description: This setting says whether clients should skip writing skybox depth when rendering skyboxes/skydomes. Skipping depth writes is required for halflife, quake2, and quake3 compat, but q1 content generally requires depth masking. Empty uses format-specific defaults.
allow_skybox.name: allow_skybox

baseskin.description: The name of the player skin to use as a fallback.
baseskin.name: baseskin

brightness.description: Brightness is how much 'white' to add to each and every pixel on the screen.
brightness.name: brightness

capturecodec.description: the compression/encoding codec to use.\nWith raw capturing, this should be one of tga,png,jpg,pcx (ie: screenshot extensions).
capturecodec.name: capturecodec

capturedemoheight.description: When using capturedemo, this specifies the height of the FBO image used.
capturedemoheight.name: capturedemoheight

capturedemowidth.description: When using capturedemo, this specifies the width of the FBO image used. Can be larger than your physical monitor.
capturedemowidth.name: capturedemowidth

capturedriver.description: The driver to use to capture the demo. Use the capture command with no arguments for a list of drivers.
capturedriver.name: capturedriver

capturerate.description: The framerate of the video to capture
capturerate.name: capturerate

capturesound.description: Enables the capturing of game voice. If not using capturedemo, this can be combined with cl_voip_test to capture your own voice.
capturesound.name: capturesound

capturethrottlesize.description: If set, capturing will slow down significantly if there is less disk space available than this cvar (in mb). This is useful when recording a stream to (ram)disk while another program is simultaneously consuming frames.
capturethrottlesize.name: capturethrottlesize

cfg_save_aliases.description: If 1, saves aliases to configs. Note that aliases sent from servers are assumed to be server-specific and are never saved (and are forgotten on map changes, too).
cfg_save_aliases.name: cfg_save_aliases

cfg_save_all.description: If 1, cfg_save ALWAYS saves all cvars. If 0, cfg_save only ever saves archived cvars. If empty, cfg_save saves all cvars only when an explicit filename was given (ie: when not used internally via quit menu options).
cfg_save_all.name: cfg_save_all

cfg_save_auto.description: If 1, the config will automatically be saved and without prompts. If 0, you'll have to save your config manually (possibly via prompts from the quit menu).
cfg_save_auto.name: cfg_save_auto

cfg_save_binds.description: If 1, saves all key bindings to configs.
cfg_save_binds.name: cfg_save_binds

cfg_save_buttons.description: If 1, saves the state of things such as +mlook or +forward to configs.
cfg_save_buttons.name: cfg_save_buttons

cfg_save_infos.description: If 1, saves userinfo and serverinfo to configs.
cfg_save_infos.name: cfg_save_infos

cfg_save_name.description: This is the config name that is saved by default when no argument is specified.
cfg_save_name.name: cfg_save_name

cl_aliasoverlap.description: Rename new aliases if they would override cvar names.
cl_aliasoverlap.name: cl_aliasoverlap

cl_autotrack.description: Specifies the default tracking mode at the start of the map. Use the 'autotrack' command to reset/apply an auto-tracking mode without changing the default.\nValid values are: high, ^hkiller^h, mod, user. Other values are treated as weighting scripts for mvd playback, where available.
cl_autotrack.name: cl_autotrack

cl_autotrack_team.description: Specifies a team name that should be auto-tracked (players on other teams will not be candidates for autotracking). Accepts * and ? wildcards for awkward chars.
cl_autotrack_team.name: cl_autotrack_team

cl_backspeed.description: The base speed that you move backwards at. If empty, uses the value of cl_forwardspeed instead.
cl_backspeed.name: cl_backspeed

cl_beam_alpha.description: Specifies the translucency of the lightning beam segments.
cl_beam_alpha.name: cl_beam_alpha

cl_beam_trace.description: Clips the length of any beams according to any walls they may have impacted.
cl_beam_trace.name: cl_beam_trace

cl_bob.description: Controls how much the camera position should bob up down as the player runs around.
cl_bob.name: cl_bob

cl_bobmodel.description: Controls whether the viewmodel should bob up and down as the player runs around.
cl_bobmodel.name: cl_bobmodel

cl_c2sImpulseBackup.description: Prevents the cl_c2spps setting from dropping redundant packets that contain impulses, in an attempt to keep impulses more reliable.
cl_c2sImpulseBackup.name: cl_c2sImpulseBackup

cl_c2sMaxRedundancy.description: This is the maximum number of input frames to send in each input packet. Values greater than 1 provide redundancy and avoid prediction misses, though you might find cl_c2sdupe provides equivelent result and at lower latency. It is locked at 3 for vanilla quakeworld, and locked at 1 for vanilla netquake.
cl_c2sMaxRedundancy.name: cl_c2sMaxRedundancy

cl_c2sdupe.description: Send duplicate copies of packets to the server. This avoids extra latency caused by packetloss, but could also make the problem worse.
cl_c2sdupe.name: cl_c2sdupe

cl_c2spps.description: Reduces outgoing packet rates by dropping up to a third of outgoing packets.
cl_c2spps.name: cl_c2spps

cl_chatmode.description:
0(nq) - everything is assumed to be a console command. prefix with 'say', or just use a messagemode bind
1(q3) - everything is assumed to be chat, unless its prefixed with a /
2(qw) - anything explicitly recognised as a command will be used as a command, anything unrecognised will be a chat message.
/ prefix is supported in all cases.
ctrl held when pressing enter always makes any implicit chat into team chat instead.
cl_chatmode.name: cl_chatmode

cl_countpendingpl.description: If set to 1, packet loss percentages will show packets still in transit as lost, even if they might still be received.
cl_countpendingpl.name: cl_countpendingpl

cl_crypt_rcon.description: Controls whether to send a hash instead of sending your rcon password as plain-text. Set to 1 for security, or 0 for backwards compatibility.\nYour command and any responses will still be sent as plain text.\nInstead, it is recommended to use rcon ONLY via dtls/tls/wss connections.
cl_crypt_rcon.name: cl_crypt_rcon

cl_defaultport.description: The default port used to connect to servers.\nQW: , NQ: , Q2: , Q3: .
cl_defaultport.name: cl_defaultport

cl_demoreel.description: When enabled, the engine will begin playing a demo loop on startup.
cl_demoreel.name: cl_demoreel

cl_dlemptyterminate.description: Terminate downloads when reciving an empty download packet. This should help work around buggy mvdsv servers.
cl_dlemptyterminate.name: cl_dlemptyterminate

cl_download_csprogs.description: Download updated client gamecode if available. Warning: If you clear this to avoid downloading vm code, you should also clear cl_download_packages.
cl_download_csprogs.name: cl_download_csprogs

cl_download_mapsrc.description: Specifies an http location prefix for map downloads. EG: \"http://example.com/path/gamemaps/\"
cl_download_mapsrc.name: cl_download_mapsrc

cl_download_packages.description: 0=Do not download packages simply because the server is using them. 1=Download and load packages as needed (does not affect games which do not use this package). 2=Do download and install permanently (use with caution!)
cl_download_packages.name: cl_download_packages

cl_download_redirection.description: Follow download redirection to download packages instead of individual files. Also allows the server to send nearly arbitary download commands.\n2: allows redirection only to named packages files (and demos/*.mvd), which is a bit safer.
cl_download_redirection.name: cl_download_redirection

cl_download_wait.description: 0=join the game before downloads have even finished (might be laggy). 1=wait for all downloads to complete before joining.
cl_download_wait.name: cl_download_wait

cl_downloads.description: Allows you to block all automatic downloads.
cl_downloads.name: cl_downloads

cl_expsprite.description: Display a central sprite in explosion effects. QuakeWorld typically does so, NQ mods should not (which is problematic when played with the qw protocol).
cl_expsprite.name: cl_expsprite

cl_fakeframes.description: Slow GPU? Want to see higher framerates get reported! Unleash the power of the lie to see much higher framerates! Many people said it couldn't be done, that the people wouldn't accept it, but to hell with the neighsayers and non-believers! WE WANT BIGGER NUMBERS AND WE'RE DAMN WELL GONNA GET THEM!... For best results, combine with an external tool like fluid motion frames...
cl_fakeframes.name: cl_fakeframes

cl_fastaccel.description: Begin moving at full speed instantly, instead of waiting a frame or so.
cl_fastaccel.name: cl_fastaccel

cl_fullpitch.description: When set, attempts to unlimit the default view pitch. Note that some servers will screw over your angles if you use this, resulting in terrible gameplay, while some may merely clamp your angle serverside. This is also considered a cheat in quakeworld, ^1so this will not function there^7. For the equivelent in quakeworld, use serverinfo minpitch+maxpitch instead, which applies to all players fairly.
cl_fullpitch.name: cl_fullpitch

cl_hightrack.description: Obsolete. If you want hightrack, use '[cl_]autotrack high' instead.
cl_hightrack.name: cl_hightrack

cl_iDrive.description: Effectively releases movement keys when the opposing key is pressed. This avoids dead-time when both keys are pressed. This can be emulated with various scripts, but that's messy.
cl_iDrive.name: cl_iDrive

cl_idlefps.description: This is the maximum framerate to attain while idle/paused/unfocused.
cl_idlefps.name: cl_idlefps

cl_legacystains.description: WARNING: this cvar will default to 0 and later removed at some point
cl_legacystains.name: cl_legacystains

cl_lerp_driftbias.description: Additional bias, can be set to a negative value to hold interpolation in the past.
cl_lerp_driftbias.name: cl_lerp_driftbias

cl_lerp_driftfrac.description: Proportion of the latest time vs the older time to favour drifting towards.
cl_lerp_driftfrac.name: cl_lerp_driftfrac

cl_lerp_maxdistance.description: Maximum distance that an entity may move between snapshots without being considered as having teleported.
cl_lerp_maxdistance.name: cl_lerp_maxdistance

cl_lerp_maxinterval.description: Maximum interval between keyframes, in seconds. Larger values can result in entities drifting very slowly when they move sporadically.
cl_lerp_maxinterval.name: cl_lerp_maxinterval

cl_lerp_players.description: Set this to make other players smoother, though it may increase effective latency. Affects only QuakeWorld.
cl_lerp_players.name: cl_lerp_players

cl_lerp_smooth.description: If 2, will act as 1 when playing demos/singleplayer and otherwise act as if set to 0 (ie: deathmatch).\nIf 1, interpolation will run in the past, resulting in really smooth movement at the cost of latency (even on bunchy german ISDNs).\nIf 0, interpolation will be based upon packet arrival times and may judder due to packet loss.
cl_lerp_smooth.name: cl_lerp_smooth

cl_loopbackprotocol.description: Which protocol to use for single-player/the internal client. Should be one of: qw, qwid, nqid, nq, fitz, bjp3, dp6, dp7, auto. If 'auto', will use qw protocols for qw mods, and nq protocols for nq mods.
cl_loopbackprotocol.name: cl_loopbackprotocol

cl_maxfps.description: Sets the maximum allowed framerate. If you're using vsync or want to uncap framerates entirely then you should probably set this to 0. Set cl_yieldcpu 0 if you're trying to benchmark.
cl_maxfps.name: cl_maxfps

cl_maxfps_slop.description: If a frame is delayed (eg because of poor system timer precision), this is how much sooner to pretend the frame happened (in milliseconds). If it is set too low then the average framerate will drop below the target, while too high may result in excessively fast frames.
cl_maxfps_slop.name: cl_maxfps_slop

cl_model_bobbing.description: Makes rotating pickup items bob too.
cl_model_bobbing.name: cl_model_bobbing

cl_movement.description: Specifies whether to send movement sequence info over DPP7 protocols (other protocols are unaffected). Unlike cl_nopred, this can result in different serverside behaviour.
cl_movement.name: cl_movement

cl_netfps.description: Send up to this many packets to the server per second. The rate used is also limited by the server which usually forces a cap to this setting of 77. Low packet rates can result in extra extrapolation to try to hide the resulting latencies.
cl_netfps.name: cl_netfps

cl_nofake.description: value 0: permits \\r chars in chat messages\nvalue 1: blocks all \\r chars\nvalue 2: allows \\r chars, but only from teammates
cl_nofake.name: cl_nofake

cl_nolerp.description: Disables interpolation. If set, missiles/monsters will be show exactly what was last received, which will be jerky. Does not affect players. A value of 2 means 'interpolate only in single-player/coop'.
cl_nolerp.name: cl_nolerp

cl_nolerp_netquake.description: Disables interpolation when connected to an NQ server. Does affect players, even the local player. You probably don't want to set this.
cl_nolerp_netquake.name: cl_nolerp_netquake

cl_parsewhitetext.description: When parsing chat messages, enable support for messages like: red{white}red
cl_parsewhitetext.name: cl_parsewhitetext

cl_part_density_fade.description: Specifies the distance over which ssqc pointparticles density fades from all to none. If this is set to 0 then particles will spawn at their normal density regardless of location on the map.
cl_part_density_fade.name: cl_part_density_fade

cl_part_density_fade_start.description: Specifies the distance at which ssqc's pointparticles will start to get less dense.
cl_part_density_fade_start.name: cl_part_density_fade_start

cl_predict_extrapolate.description: If 1, enables prediction based upon partial input frames which can change over time resulting in a swimmy feel but does not need to interpolate. If 0, prediction will stay in the past and thus use only completed frames. Interpolation will then be used to smooth movement.\nThis cvar only applies when video and input frames are independant (ie: cl_netfps is set).
cl_predict_extrapolate.name: cl_predict_extrapolate

cl_predict_players.description: Clear this cvar to see ents exactly how they are on the server.
cl_predict_players.name: cl_predict_players

cl_predict_players_frac.description: How much of other players to predict. Values less than 1 will help minimize overruns.
cl_predict_players_frac.name: cl_predict_players_frac

cl_predict_players_latency.description: Push the player back according to your latency, to give a smooth consistent simulation of the server.
cl_predict_players_latency.name: cl_predict_players_latency

cl_predict_players_nudge.description: An extra nudge of time, to cover video latency.
cl_predict_players_nudge.name: cl_predict_players_nudge

cl_predict_timenudge.description: A debug feature. You should normally leave this as 0. Nudges local player prediction into the future if positive (resulting in extrapolation), or into the past if negative (resulting in laggy interpolation). Value is in seconds, so small decimals are required. This cvar applies even if input frames are tied to video frames.
cl_predict_timenudge.name: cl_predict_timenudge

cl_pure.description:
0=standard quake rules.
1=clients should prefer files within packages present on the server.
2=clients should use *only* files within packages present on the server.
Due to quake 1.01/1.06 differences, a setting of 2 is only reliable with total conversions.
If sv_pure is set, the client will prefer the highest value set.
cl_pure.name: cl_pure

cl_queueimpulses.description: Queues unsent impulses instead of replacing them. This avoids the need for extra wait commands (and the timing issues of such commands), but potentially increases latency and can cause scripts to be desynced with regard to buttons and impulses.
cl_queueimpulses.name: cl_queueimpulses

cl_r2g.description: Uses progs/grenade.mdl instead of progs/missile.mdl when 1.
cl_r2g.name: cl_r2g

cl_rollalpha.description: Controls the speed at which the view rolls according to sideways movement.
cl_rollalpha.name: cl_rollalpha

cl_rollangle.description: Controls the maximum view should tilt while strafing.
cl_rollangle.name: cl_rollangle

cl_rollspeed.description: Controls the speed required to reach cl_rollangle's tilt.
cl_rollspeed.name: cl_rollspeed

cl_run.description: Enables autorun, inverting the state of the +speed key.
cl_run.name: cl_run

cl_sbaralpha.description: Specifies the transparency of the status bar. Only Takes effect when cl_sbar is set to 2.
cl_sbaralpha.name: cl_sbaralpha

cl_sendchatstate.description: Announce your chat state to the server in a privacy-violating kind of way. This allows other players to see your afk/at-console status.
cl_sendchatstate.name: cl_sendchatstate

cl_sendguid.description: Send a randomly generated 'globally unique' id to servers, which can be used by servers for score rankings and stuff. Different servers will see different guids. Delete the 'qkey' file in order to appear as a different user.\nIf set to 2, all servers will see the same guid. Be warned that this can show other people the guid that you're using.
cl_sendguid.name: cl_sendguid

cl_serveraddress.description: The address of the last server you connected to
cl_serveraddress.name: cl_serveraddress

cl_servername.description: The hostname of the last server you connected to
cl_servername.name: cl_servername

cl_shownet.description: Debugging var. 0 shows nothing. 1 shows incoming packet sizes. 2 shows individual messages. 3 shows entities too.
cl_shownet.name: cl_shownet

cl_smartjump.description: Makes the jump button act as +moveup when in water. This is typically quieter and faster.
cl_smartjump.name: cl_smartjump

cl_solid_players.description: Consider other players as solid for player prediction.
cl_solid_players.name: cl_solid_players

cl_splitscreen.description: Enables splitscreen support. See also: allow_splitscreen, in_rawinput*, the \"p\" command.
cl_splitscreen.name: cl_splitscreen

cl_standardchat.description: Disables auto colour coding in chat messages.
cl_standardchat.name: cl_standardchat

cl_standardmsg.description: Disables auto colour coding in console prints.
cl_standardmsg.name: cl_standardmsg

cl_threadedphysics.description: When set, client input frames are generated and sent on a worker thread
cl_threadedphysics.name: cl_threadedphysics

cl_truelightning.description: Manipulate the end position of the player's own beams, to hide lag. Can be set to fractional values to reduce the effect.
cl_truelightning.name: cl_truelightning

cl_verify_urischeme.description: 0: Do nothing.\n1: Check whether our protocol scheme is registered and prompt the user to register associations.\n2: Always re-register on every startup, without prompting. Sledgehammer style.
cl_verify_urischeme.name: cl_verify_urischeme

cl_voip_autogain.description: Attempts to normalize your voice levels to a standard level. Useful for lazy people, but interferes with voice activation levels.
cl_voip_autogain.name: cl_voip_autogain

cl_voip_bitrate.description: For codecs with non-specific bitrates, this specifies the target bitrate to use.
cl_voip_bitrate.name: cl_voip_bitrate

cl_voip_capturingvol.description: Volume multiplier applied while capturing, to avoid your audio from being heard by others. Does not affect game volume when others speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).
cl_voip_capturingvol.name: cl_voip_capturingvol

cl_voip_codec.description: 0: speex(@11khz). 1: raw. 2: opus. 3: speex(@8khz). 4: speex(@16). 5:speex(@32). 6: pcma. 7: pcmu.
cl_voip_codec.name: cl_voip_codec

cl_voip_ducking.description: Scales game audio by this much when someone is talking to you. Does not affect your speaker volume when you speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).
cl_voip_ducking.name: cl_voip_ducking

cl_voip_micamp.description: Amplifies your microphone when using voip.
cl_voip_micamp.name: cl_voip_micamp

cl_voip_noisefilter.description: Enable the use of the noise cancelation filter.
cl_voip_noisefilter.name: cl_voip_noisefilter

cl_voip_play.description: Enables voip playback. Value is a volume scaler.
cl_voip_play.name: cl_voip_play

cl_voip_send.description:
Sends voice-over-ip data to the server whenever it is set.
0: only send voice if +voip is pressed.
1: voice activation.
2: constantly send.
+4: Do not send to game, only to rtp sessions.
cl_voip_send.name: cl_voip_send

cl_voip_showmeter.description: Shows your speech volume above the standard hud. 0=hide, 1=show when transmitting, 2=ignore voice-activation disable
cl_voip_showmeter.name: cl_voip_showmeter

cl_voip_test.description: If 1, enables you to hear your own voice directly, bypassing the server and thus without networking latency, but is fine for checking audio levels. Note that sv_voip_echo can be set if you want to include latency and packetloss considerations, but setting that cvar requires server admin access and is thus much harder to use.
cl_voip_test.name: cl_voip_test

cl_voip_vad_delay.description: Keeps sending voice data for this many seconds after voice activation would normally stop
cl_voip_vad_delay.name: cl_voip_vad_delay

cl_voip_vad_threshhold.description: This is the threshhold for voice-activation-detection when sending voip data
cl_voip_vad_threshhold.name: cl_voip_vad_threshhold

cl_vrui_force.description: Force the use of VR UIs, even with no VR headset active.
cl_vrui_force.name: cl_vrui_force

cl_vrui_lock.description: Controls how the UI is positioned when using VR/XR. 0: Repositioned infront of the head when the console/menus are toggled. 1: Locked infront of the reference position (which may require the user to turn around to find it).
cl_vrui_lock.name: cl_vrui_lock

cl_weaponforgetorder.description: The 'weapon' command will lock in its weapon choice, instead of choosing a different weapon between select+fire.
cl_weaponforgetorder.name: cl_weaponforgetorder

cl_weaponhide.description:
HACK: Attempt to switch weapon to another in order to cheat your killer out of any possible weapon upgrades.
0: original behaviour
1: switch away when +attack/+fire is released
2: switch away only in deathmatch
cl_weaponhide.name: cl_weaponhide

cl_weaponhide_preference.description: The weapon you would like to try to switch to when cl_weaponhide is active
cl_weaponhide_preference.name: cl_weaponhide_preference

cl_yieldcpu.description: Attempt to yield between frames. This can resolve issues with certain drivers and background software, but can mean less consistant frame times. Will reduce power consumption/heat generation so should be set on laptops or similar (over-hot/battery powered) devices.

com_fullgamename.description: The filesystem is trying to run this game
com_fullgamename.name: com_fullgamename

com_highlightcolor.description: ANSI colour to be used for highlighted text, used when com_parseutf8 is active.
com_highlightcolor.name: com_highlightcolor

com_parseutf8.description: Interpret console messages/playernames/etc as UTF-8. Requires special fonts. -1=iso 8859-1. 0=quakeascii(chat uses high chars). 1=utf8, revert to ascii on decode errors. 2=utf8 ignoring errors
com_parseutf8.name: com_parseutf8

com_protocolname.description: The protocol game name used for dpmaster queries. For compatibility with DP, you can set this to 'DarkPlaces-Quake' in order to be listed in DP's master server, and to list DP servers.
com_protocolname.name: com_protocolname

com_protocolversion.description: The protocol version used for dpmaster queries.
com_protocolversion.name: com_protocolversion

con_logcenterprint.description:
Specifies whether to print centerprints on the console.
0: never
1: single-player or coop only.
2: always.
con_logcenterprint.name: con_logcenterprint

con_stayhidden.description:
0: allow console to pounce on the user
1: console stays hidden unless explicitly invoked
2:toggleconsole command no longer works
3: shift+escape key no longer works
con_stayhidden.name: con_stayhidden

con_textfont.description: Specifies the font file to use. a value such as FONT:ALTFONT specifies an alternative font to be used when ^^a is used.\nWhen using TTF fonts, you will likely need to scale text to at least 150% - vid_conautoscale 1.5 will do this.\nTTF fonts may be loaded from your windows directory. \'gl_font cour?col=1,1,1:couri?col=0,1,0\' loads eg: c:\\windows\\fonts\\cour.ttf, and uses the italic version of courier for alternative text, with specific colour tints.
con_textfont.name: con_textfont

con_textsize.description: Resize the console text to be a different height, scaled separately from the hud. The value is the height in (virtual) pixels.
con_textsize.name: con_textsize

con_window.description: States whether the console should be a floating window as in source engine games, or a top-of-the-screen-only thing.
con_window.name: con_window

contrast.description: Scales colour values linearly to make your screen easier to see. Setting this to anything but 1 without hardware gamma will reduce your framerates a little.
contrast.name: contrast

crosshaircorrect.description: Moves the crosshair around to represent the impact point of a weapon positioned below the actual view position.
crosshaircorrect.name: crosshaircorrect

crosshairimage.description: Enables the use of an external/custom crosshair image
crosshairimage.name: crosshairimage

d_lodbias.description: Biases choice of mipmap levels. Positive values will give more blury textures, while negative values will give crisper images (but will also give some mid-surface aliasing artifacts).
d_lodbias.name: d_lodbias

d_mipcap.description: Specifies the range of mipmap levels to use.
d_mipcap.name: d_mipcap

developer.description: Enables the spewing of additional developer/debugging messages. 2 will give even more spam, much of it unwanted.
developer.name: developer

dpcompat_console.description: Enables hacks to emulate DP's console.
dpcompat_console.name: dpcompat_console

dpcompat_csqcinputeventtypes.description: Specifies the first csqc input event that the mod does not recognise. This should never have been a thing, but some mods are simply too buggy.
dpcompat_csqcinputeventtypes.name: dpcompat_csqcinputeventtypes

dpcompat_findradiusarealinks.description: Use the world collision info to accelerate findradius instead of looping through every single entity. May actually be slower for large radiuses, or fail to find entities which have not been linked properly with setorigin.
dpcompat_findradiusarealinks.name: dpcompat_findradiusarealinks

dpcompat_nofloodfill.description: Disables the q1mdl floodfill. Setting this to 1 may result in blue seams on the vanilla quake models.
dpcompat_nofloodfill.name: dpcompat_nofloodfill

dpcompat_nopremulpics.description: By default FTE uses premultiplied alpha for hud/2d images, while DP does not (which results in halos with low-res content). Unfortunately DDS files would need to be recompressed, resulting in visible issues.
dpcompat_nopremulpics.name: dpcompat_nopremulpics

dpcompat_nopreparse.description: Xonotic uses svc_tempentity with unknowable lengths mixed with other data that needs to be translated. This cvar disables any attempt to translate or pre-parse network messages, including disabling nq/qw cross compatibility. NOTE: because preparsing will be disabled, messages might not get backbuffered correctly if too much reliable data is written.
dpcompat_nopreparse.name: dpcompat_nopreparse

dpcompat_noretouchground.description: Prevents entities that are already standing on an entity from touching the same entity again.
dpcompat_noretouchground.name: dpcompat_noretouchground

dpcompat_precachesoundhack.description: Changes the behaviour of only the ssqc's precache_sound to return a precache index. precache_model and csqc's precaches are unchanged.
dpcompat_precachesoundhack.name: dpcompat_precachesoundhack

dpcompat_skinfiles.description: When set, uses a nodraw shader for any unmentioned surfaces.
dpcompat_skinfiles.name: dpcompat_skinfiles

dpcompat_smallerfonts.description: Mimics DP's behaviour of using a smaller font size than was actually requested.
dpcompat_smallerfonts.name: dpcompat_smallerfonts

dpcompat_strcat_limit.description: When set, cripples strcat (and related function) string lengths to the value specified.\nSet to 16383 to replicate DP's limit, otherwise leave as 0 to avoid limits.
dpcompat_strcat_limit.name: dpcompat_strcat_limit

drate.description: A rough measure of the bandwidth to try to use while downloading (in bytes per second).
drate.name: drate

dtls_psk_hint.description: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the public server identity.
dtls_psk_hint.name: dtls_psk_hint

dtls_psk_key.description: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the hexadecimal key which must match between client+server. Will only be used when client+server's hint settings match.
dtls_psk_key.name: dtls_psk_key

dtls_psk_user.description: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the username to use when the client+server's hints match.
dtls_psk_user.name: dtls_psk_user

edit_addcr.description: make sure that each line ends with a \\r (on save). Empty will be assumed to be 1 on windows and 0 otherwise.
edit_addcr.name: edit_addcr

ezcompat_markup.description: Attempt compatibility with ezquake's text markup.0: disabled.\n1: Handle markup ampersand markup.\n2: Handle chevron markup (only in echo commands, for config compat, because its just too unreliable otherwise).
ezcompat_markup.name: ezcompat_markup

ffov.description: Allows you to set a specific field of view for when a custom projection is specified. If empty, will use regular fov cvar, which might get messy.
ffov.name: ffov

filterban.description: If 0, players will be kicked by default unless there is a rule that allows them. Also affects the default action of addip.
filterban.name: filterban

fov.description: field of vision, 1-170 degrees, standard fov is 90, nquake defaults to 108.
fov.name: fov

fraglog_details.description:
Bitmask
1: killer+killee names.
2: killer+killee teams
4:timestamp.
8:killer weapon
16:killer+killee guid.
For compatibility, use 1(vanilla) or 7(mvdsv).
fraglog_details.name: fraglog_details

fraglog_public.description: Enables support for connectionless fraglog requests
fraglog_public.name: fraglog_public

fs_basepath.description: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the base directory.
fs_basepath.name: fs_basepath

fs_cache.description: 0: Do individual lookups.\n1: Scan all files for accelerated lookups. This provides a performance boost on windows and avoids case sensitivity issues on linux.\n2: like 1, but don't bother checking for external changes (avoiding the cost of rebuild the cache).
fs_cache.name: fs_cache

fs_game.description: Provided for Q2 compat. Contains the subdir of the current mod.
fs_game.name: fs_game

fs_gamepath.description: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the active gamedir.
fs_gamepath.name: fs_gamepath

fs_hidesyspaths.description: 0: Show system paths in console prints that might appear in screenshots or video capture.\n1: Replace the start of filenames in console prints with generic prefixes that cannot leak private info like your operating system's user name.
fs_hidesyspaths.name: fs_hidesyspaths

fs_homepath.description: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the base directory.
fs_homepath.name: fs_homepath

fs_noreexec.description: Disables automatic re-execing configs on gamedir switches.\nThis means your cvar defaults etc may be from the wrong mod, and cfg_save will leave that stuff corrupted!
fs_noreexec.name: fs_noreexec

fs_packageprioritisation.description: Favours the package that is:\n0: Most recently modified\n1: Is alphabetically last (favour z over a, 9 over 0).
fs_packageprioritisation.name: fs_packageprioritisation

gamma.description: Controls how bright the screen is. Setting this to anything but 1 without hardware gamma requires glsl support and can noticably harm your framerate.
gamma.name: gamma

gl_affinemodels.description: Use affine texture sampling for models. This replicates software rendering's distortions.
gl_affinemodels.name: gl_affinemodels

gl_blacklist_generatemipmap.description: Self-generate mipmaps, instead of letting the graphics driver do it.
gl_blacklist_generatemipmap.name: gl_blacklist_generatemipmap

gl_blacklist_texture_compression.description: When enabled, blocks recognition of all compressed-texture formats. Does NOT block support for gl3 texture types like e5bgr9 nor rgba16f.
gl_blacklist_texture_compression.name: gl_blacklist_texture_compression

gl_blendsprites.description:
Specifies how sprites are blended.
0: Alpha tested.
1: Premultiplied blend.
2: Additive blend.
gl_blendsprites.name: gl_blendsprites

gl_compress.description: Enable automatic texture compression even for textures which are not pre-compressed.
gl_compress.name: gl_compress

gl_conback.description: Specifies which conback shader/image to use. The Quake fallback is gfx/conback.lmp
gl_conback.name: gl_conback

gl_driver.description: Specifies the graphics driver name to load. This is typically a filename. Blank for default.
gl_driver.name: gl_driver

gl_font.description: Specifies the font file to use. a value such as FONT:ALTFONT specifies an alternative font to be used when ^^a is used.\nWhen using TTF fonts, you will likely need to scale text to at least 150% - vid_conautoscale 1.5 will do this.\nTTF fonts may be loaded from your windows directory. \'gl_font cour?col=1,1,1:couri?col=0,1,0\' loads eg: c:\\windows\\fonts\\cour.ttf, and uses the italic version of courier for alternative text, with specific colour tints.
gl_font.name: gl_font

gl_immutable_buffers.description: Controls whether to use immutable GPU memory allocations for static OpenGL vertex buffers. This potentially means less work for the drivers and thus higher framerates.
gl_immutable_buffers.name: gl_immutable_buffers

gl_immutable_textures.description: Controls whether to use immutable GPU memory allocations for OpenGL textures. This potentially means less work for the drivers and thus higher framerates.
gl_immutable_textures.name: gl_immutable_textures

gl_lerpimages.description: Enables smoother resampling for images which are not power-of-two, when the drivers do not support non-power-of-two textures.
gl_lerpimages.name: gl_lerpimages

gl_lightmap_average.description: Determine lightmap values based upon the center of the polygon. This will give a more buggy look, quite probably.
gl_lightmap_average.name: gl_lightmap_average

gl_lightmap_nearest.description: Use nearest sampling for lightmaps. This will give a more blocky look. Meaningless when gl_lightmap_average is enabled.
gl_lightmap_nearest.name: gl_lightmap_nearest

gl_max_size.description: Specifies the maximum texture size that the engine may use. Textures larger than this will be downsized. Clamped by the value the driver supports.
gl_max_size.name: gl_max_size

gl_maxdist.description: The distance of the far clip plane. If set to 0, some fancy maths will be used to place it at an infinite distance.
gl_maxdist.name: gl_maxdist

gl_menutint_shader.description: Controls the use of GLSL to desaturate the background when drawing the menu, like quake's dos software renderer used to do before the ugly dithering of winquake.
gl_menutint_shader.name: gl_menutint_shader

gl_mindist.description: Distance to the near clip plane. Smaller values may damage depth precision, high values can potentialy be used to see through walls...
gl_mindist.name: gl_mindist

gl_nocolors.description: Ignores player colours and skins, reducing texture memory usage at the cost of not knowing whether you're killing your team mates.
gl_nocolors.name: gl_nocolors

gl_nohwblend.description: If 1, don't use hardware gamma ramps for transient effects that change each frame (does not affect long-term effects like holding quad or underwater tints).
gl_nohwblend.name: gl_nohwblend

gl_overbright_models.description: Doubles the brightness of models, to match QuakeSpasm's misfeature of the same name.
gl_overbright_models.name: gl_overbright_models

gl_part_flame.description: Enable particle emitting from models. Mainly used for torch and flame effects.
gl_part_flame.name: gl_part_flame

gl_pbolightmaps.description: Controls whether to use PBOs for streaming lightmap updates. This prevents CPU stalls while the driver reads out the lightmap data (lightmap updates are still not free though).
gl_pbolightmaps.name: gl_pbolightmaps

gl_picmip.description: Reduce world/model texture sizes by some exponential factor.
gl_picmip.name: gl_picmip

gl_picmip2d.description: Reduce hud/menu texture sizes by some exponential factor.
gl_picmip2d.name: gl_picmip2d

gl_picmip_other.description: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of model textures.
gl_picmip_other.name: gl_picmip_other

gl_picmip_sprites.description: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of sprite textures.
gl_picmip_sprites.name: gl_picmip_sprites

gl_picmip_world.description: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of world textures.
gl_picmip_world.name: gl_picmip_world

gl_polyblend.description: Controls whether temporary whole-screen colour changes should be honoured or not. Change gl_cshiftpercent if you want to adjust the intensity.\nThis does not affect v_cshift commands sent from the server.
gl_polyblend.name: gl_polyblend

gl_polyblend_edgesize.description: This constrains colour shifts to the edge of the screen, with the value specifying the size of those borders.
gl_polyblend_edgesize.name: gl_polyblend_edgesize

gl_shadeq1_name.description: Rename all surfaces from quake1 bsps using this pattern for the purposes of shader names.
gl_shadeq1_name.name: gl_shadeq1_name

gl_skyboxdist.description: The distance of the skybox. If 0, the engine will determine it based upon the far clip plane distance.
gl_skyboxdist.name: gl_skyboxdist

gl_texture_anisotropy.description: Allows for higher quality textures on surfaces that slope away from the camera (like the floor). Set to 16 or something. Only supported with trilinear filtering.
gl_texture_anisotropy.name: gl_texture_anisotropy

gl_texturemode.description:
Specifies how world/model textures appear. Typically 3 letters eg nll or lll.
First letter can be l(inear) or n(earest) and says how to upscale low-res textures (n for the classic look - often favoured for embedded textures, l for blurry - best for high-res textures).
The middle letter can be set to '.' to disable mipmaps, or n for ugly banding with distance, or l for smooth mipmap transitions.
The third letter says what to do when the texture is too high resolution, and should generally be set to 'l' to reduce sparkles including when aiming for the classic lego look.
gl_texturemode.name: gl_texturemode

gl_texturemode2d.description: Specifies how 2d images are sampled. format is a 3-tupple
gl_texturemode2d.name: gl_texturemode2d

gl_workaround_ati_shadersource.description: Work around ATI driver bugs in the glShaderSource function. Can safely be enabled with other drivers too.
gl_workaround_ati_shadersource.name: gl_workaround_ati_shadersource

ignore_flood.description:
Provides a way to reduce inbound spam from flooding out your chat (dupe messages are ignored).
0: No inbound flood protection.
1: Duplicate non-team messages will be filtered.
2: ALL duplicate messages will be filtered
ignore_flood.name: ignore_flood

ignore_flood_duration.description: Time limit for inbound messages to be considered duplicates.
ignore_flood_duration.name: ignore_flood_duration

ignore_opponents.description:
0: Don't ignore chat from enemies.
1: Always ignore chat from opponents (note: can also ignore f_ruleset checks).
2: Ignore chat from opponents only during a match (requires servers that actually reports match state).

ignore_spec.description: 0: Never ignore spectators.\n1: Ignore spectators only when playing.\n2: Always ignore spectators even when spectating.

in_dinput.description: Enables the use of dinput for mouse movements
in_dinput.name: in_dinput

in_forceseat.description: Overrides the device identifiers to control a specific client from any device. This can be used for debugging mods, where you only have one keyboard/mouse.
in_forceseat.name: in_forceseat

in_nonstandarddeadkeys.description: Discard input events that result in multiple keys. Only the last key will be used. This results in behaviour that differs from eg notepad. To use a dead key, press it twice instead of the dead key followed by space.
in_nonstandarddeadkeys.name: in_nonstandarddeadkeys

in_rawinput.description: Enables rawinput support for mice in XP onwards. Rawinput permits independant device identification (ie: splitscreen clients can each have their own mouse)
in_rawinput.name: in_rawinput

in_rawinput_keyboard.description: Enables rawinput support for keyboards in XP onwards as well as just mice.
in_rawinput_keyboard.name: in_rawinput_keyboard

in_rawinput_rdp.description: Activate Remote Desktop Protocol devices too.
in_rawinput_rdp.name: in_rawinput_rdp

in_skipplayerone.description: Do not auto-assign joysticks/game-controllers to the first player. Requires in_restart to take effect.
in_skipplayerone.name: in_skipplayerone

in_vraim.description: When set to 1, the 'view' angle sent to the server is controlled by your vr headset instead of separately. This is for fallback behaviour and blocks mouse+joy+gamepad aiming.
in_vraim.name: in_vraim

in_xinput.description: Enables the use of xinput for controllers.\nNote that if you have a headset plugged in, that headset will be used for audio playback if no specific audio device is configured.
in_xinput.name: in_xinput

ipautodump.description: Enables dumping the 'iplog.txt' file, which contains a log of usernames seen for a given IP, which is useful for detecting fake-nicks.
ipautodump.name: ipautodump

joyexponent.description: Scales joystick/controller sensitivity non-linearly to increase precision in the center.\nA value of 1 is linear.
joyexponent.name: joyexponent

joyradialdeadzone.description:
Treat controller dead zones as a pair, rather than per-axis.
0: treat joystick axis independantly (square).
1: treat the axis together, radially.
2: do not handle deadzones (prefiltered).
joyradialdeadzone.name: joyradialdeadzone

lang.description: This cvar contains the language_dialect code of your language, used to find localisation strings.
lang.name: lang

log_developer.description: Enables logging of console prints when set to 1. Otherwise unimportant messages will not fill up your log files.
log_developer.name: log_developer

log_readable.description:
Bitfield describing what to convert/strip. If 0, exact byte representation will be used.
&1: Dequakify text.
&2: Strip special markup.
&4: Strip ansi control codes.
log_readable.name: log_readable

lookspring.description: Recentre the camera when the mouse-look is released.
lookspring.name: lookspring

m_accel.description: Values >0 will amplify mouse movement proportional to velocity. Small values have great effect. A lot of good Quake Live players use around the 0.1-0.2 mark, but this depends on your mouse CPI and polling rate.
m_accel.name: m_accel

m_accel_offset.description: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nAcceleration will not be active until the mouse movement exceeds this speed (counts per millisecond). Negative values are supported, which has the effect of causing higher rates of acceleration to happen at lower velocities.
m_accel_offset.name: m_accel_offset

m_accel_power.description: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nValues 1 or below are dumb. 2 is linear and the default. 99% of accel users use this. Above 2 begins to amplify exponentially and you will get more acceleration at higher velocities. Great if you want low accel for slow movements, and high accel for fast movements. Good in combination with a sensitivity cap.
m_accel_power.name: m_accel_power

m_accel_senscap.description: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nSets an upper limit on the amplified mouse movement. Great for tuning acceleration around lower velocities while still remaining in control of fast motion such as flicking.
m_accel_senscap.name: m_accel_senscap

m_accel_style.description: 1 = Quake Live mouse acceleration, 0 = Old style accelertion.
m_accel_style.name: m_accel_style

m_forcewheel.description: 0: ignore mousewheels in apis where it is abiguous.\n1: Use mousewheel when it is treated as a third axis. Motion above a threshold is ignored, to avoid issues with an unknown threshold.\n2: Like 1, but excess motion is retained. The threshold specifies exact z-axis distance per notice.
m_forcewheel.name: m_forcewheel

m_forcewheel_threshold.description: Mousewheel graduations smaller than this will not trigger mousewheel deltas.
m_forcewheel_threshold.name: m_forcewheel_threshold

m_longpressthreshold.description: How long to press for it to register as a long press (touchscreens).
m_longpressthreshold.name: m_longpressthreshold

m_slidethreshold.description: How far your finger needs to move to be considered a slide event (touchscreens).
m_slidethreshold.name: m_slidethreshold

m_touchmajoraxis.description: When using a touchscreen, use only the major axis for strafing.
m_touchmajoraxis.name: m_touchmajoraxis

m_touchstrafe.description: 0: entire screen changes angles only.\n1: right hand side controls strafing.\n2:left hand side strafes.
m_touchstrafe.name: m_touchstrafe

map_autoopenportals.description: When set to 1, force-opens all area portals. Normally these start closed and are opened by doors when they move, but this requires the gamecode to signal this.
map_autoopenportals.name: map_autoopenportals

mapname.description: Cvar that holds the short name of the current map, for scripting type stuff
mapname.name: mapname

mastervolume.description: Additional multiplier for all other sounds.
mastervolume.name: mastervolume

maxclients.description: Specify the maximum number of players allowed on the server at once. Can be changed mid-map.
maxclients.name: maxclients

maxspectators.description: Specify the maximum number of spectators allowed on the server at once. Can be changed mid-map.
maxspectators.name: maxspectators

mod_external_vis.description: Attempt to load .vis patches for quake maps, allowing transparent water to work properly.
mod_external_vis.name: mod_external_vis

mod_h2holey_bugged.description: Hexen2's holey-model flag uses index 0 as transparent (and additionally 255 in gl, due to a bug). GLQuake engines tend to have bugs that use ONLY index 255, resulting in a significant compatibility issue that can be resolved only with this shitty cvar hack.
mod_h2holey_bugged.name: mod_h2holey_bugged

mod_halftexel.description: Offset texture coords by a half-texel, for compatibility with glquake and the majority of engine forks.
mod_halftexel.name: mod_halftexel

mod_lightpoint_distance.description: This is the maximum distance to trace when searching for a ground surface for lighting info on map formats without light more fancy lighting info. Use 2048 for full compat with Quake.
mod_lightpoint_distance.name: mod_lightpoint_distance

mod_lightscale_broken.description: When active, replicates a bug from vanilla - the radius of r_dynamic lights is scaled by per-surface texture scale rather than using actual distance.
mod_lightscale_broken.name: mod_lightscale_broken

mod_litsprites_force.description: If set to 1, sprites will be lit according to world lighting (including rtlights), like Tenebrae. Ideally use EF_ADDITIVE or EF_FULLBRIGHT to make emissive sprites instead.
mod_litsprites_force.name: mod_litsprites_force

mod_loadmappackages.description: Load additional content embedded within bsp files.
mod_loadmappackages.name: mod_loadmappackages

mod_map_texscale.description: Defines the scale of texture texels. Use 1 for quake+quake2 maps, and 0.5 for quake3 maps.
mod_map_texscale.name: mod_map_texscale

mod_md3flags.description: The flags field of md3s was never officially defined. If this is set to 1, the flags will be treated identically to mdl files. Otherwise they will be ignored. Naturally, this is required to provide rotating pickups in quake.
mod_md3flags.name: mod_md3flags

mod_md5_singleanimation.description: When loading an md5mesh file, also attempt to load an .md5anim file, and unpack it into individual poses. Use 0 for mods that will be precaching their own md5anims for use with skeletal objects.
mod_md5_singleanimation.name: mod_md5_singleanimation

mod_nomipmap.description: Disables the use of mipmaps on quake1 mdls, consistent with its original software renderer.
mod_nomipmap.name: mod_nomipmap

mod_obj_orientation.description:
Controls how the model's axis are interpreted.
0: x=forward, z=up (Quake)
1: x=forward, y=up
2: z=forward, y=up
mod_obj_orientation.name: mod_obj_orientation

mod_precache.description:
Controls when models are loaded.
0: Load them only when they're actually needed.
1: Load them upfront.
2: Lazily load them to shorten load times at the risk of brief stuttering during only the start of the map.
mod_precache.name: mod_precache

mod_terrain_defaulttexture.description: Newly created terrain tiles will use this texture. This should generally be updated by the terrain editor.
mod_terrain_defaulttexture.name: mod_terrain_defaulttexture

mod_terrain_networked.description: Terrain edits are networked. Clients will download sections on demand, and servers will notify clients of changes.
mod_terrain_networked.name: mod_terrain_networked

mod_terrain_savever.description: Which terrain section version to write if terrain was edited.
mod_terrain_savever.name: mod_terrain_savever

mod_terrain_shadow_dist.description: How far rays should be cast in order to look for occlusing geometry.
mod_terrain_shadow_dist.name: mod_terrain_shadow_dist

mod_terrain_shadows.description: Cast rays to determine whether parts of the terrain should be in shadow.
mod_terrain_shadows.name: mod_terrain_shadows

mod_terrain_sundir.description: The direction of the sun (vector will be normalised).
mod_terrain_sundir.name: mod_terrain_sundir

mod_warnmodels.description: Warn if any models failed to load. Set to 0 if your mod is likely to lack optional models (like its in development).
mod_warnmodels.name: mod_warnmodels

msg.description: Filter console prints/messages. Only functions on QuakeWorld servers. 0=pickup messages. 1=death messages. 2=critical messages. 3=chat.
msg.name: msg

msg_filter.description: Filter out chat messages: 0=neither. 1=broadcast chat. 2=team chat. 3=all chat.
msg_filter.name: msg_filter

msg_filter_frags.description: Prevents frag messages from appearing on the console.
msg_filter_frags.name: msg_filter_frags

msg_filter_pickups.description: Prevents pickup messages from appearing on the console. This would normally be filtered by 'msg 1', but nq servers cannot respect that (nor nq mods running in qw servers).
msg_filter_pickups.name: msg_filter_pickups

net_compress.description: Enables huffman compression of network packets.
net_compress.name: net_compress

net_dns_ipv4.description: If 0, disables dns resolution of names to ipv4 addresses (removing any associated error messages). Also hides ipv4 addresses in address:port listings.
net_dns_ipv4.name: net_dns_ipv4

net_dns_ipv6.description: If 0, disables dns resolution of names to ipv6 addresses (removing any associated error messages). Also hides ipv6 addresses in address:port listings.
net_dns_ipv6.name: net_dns_ipv6

net_enable_.description: If enabled, accept connection requests from the quake2-remaster engine on our listening udp ports.\nNote that this defaults to disabled due to it being highly vulnerable to applification attacks.
net_enable_.name: net_enable_

net_enable_dtls.description:
Controls serverside dtls support.
0: dtls blocked, not advertised.
1: clientside choice.
2: used where possible (recommended setting).
3: disallow non-dtls clients (sv_port_tcp should be eg tls://[::]:27500 to also disallow unencrypted tcp connections).
net_enable_dtls.name: net_enable_dtls

net_enable_http.description: If enabled, tcp ports will accept inbound http clients, potentially serving large files which could distrupt gameplay (This does not affect outgoing http(s) requests).
net_enable_http.name: net_enable_http

net_enable_qizmo.description: Enables serverside support for 'connect tcp://foo' or 'connect tls://foo' (with net_enable_tls), as well as qizmo's tcp connections and compatibles.
net_enable_qizmo.name: net_enable_qizmo

net_enable_qtv.description:
Controls whether inbound qtv requests will be honoured (both proxies and clients using qtvplay).
0: Don't accept qtv connections.
1: Accept connections.
2: Accept qtv connections only from host-scopped addresses (read: 127.*.*.*, ::1, or unix sockets).
net_enable_qtv.name: net_enable_qtv

net_enable_rtcbroker.description: If 1, tcp ports will accept websocket connections from clients trying to broker direct webrtc connections. This should be low traffic, but might involve a lot of mostly-idle connections.
net_enable_rtcbroker.name: net_enable_rtcbroker

net_enable_tls.description: If enabled, binary data sent to a non-tls tcp port will be interpretted as a tls handshake (enabling https or wss over the same tcp port.
net_enable_tls.name: net_enable_tls

net_enable_websockets.description: If enabled, tcp ports will accept websocket game clients.
net_enable_websockets.name: net_enable_websockets

net_enabled.description: If 0, disables all network access, including name resolution and socket creation. Does not affect loopback/internal connections.
net_enabled.name: net_enabled

net_fakeloss.description: Simulates packetloss in both receiving and sending, on a scale from 0 to 1.
net_fakeloss.name: net_fakeloss

net_hybriddualstack.description: Uses hybrid ipv4+ipv6 sockets where possible. Not supported on xp or below.
net_hybriddualstack.name: net_hybriddualstack

net_ice_allowmdns.description: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents the use of multicast-dns to obtain candidates using random numbers instead of revealing private network info.
net_ice_allowmdns.name: net_ice_allowmdns

net_ice_allowstun.description: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents the use of stun to determine our public address (does not prevent connecting to our peer's server-reflexive candidates).
net_ice_allowstun.name: net_ice_allowstun

net_ice_allowturn.description: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents registration of turn connections (does not prevent connecting to our peer's relay candidates).
net_ice_allowturn.name: net_ice_allowturn

net_ice_broker.description: This is the default broker we attempt to connect through when using 'sv_public /foo' or 'connect /foo'.
net_ice_broker.name: net_ice_broker

net_ice_debug.description: 0: Hide messy details.\n1: Show new candidates.\n2: Show each connectivity test.
net_ice_debug.name: net_ice_debug

net_ice_exchangeprivateips.description: Boolean. When set to 0, hides private IP addresses from your peers - only addresses determined from the other side of your router will be shared. You should only need to set this to 1 if mdns is unavailable.
net_ice_exchangeprivateips.name: net_ice_exchangeprivateips

net_ice_relayonly.description: Boolean. When set to 1, blocks reporting non-relay local candidates, does not attempt to connect to remote candidates other than via a relay.
net_ice_relayonly.name: net_ice_relayonly

net_ice_servers.description: A space-separated list of ICE servers, eg stun:host.example:3478 or turn:host.example:3478?user=foo?auth=blah
net_ice_servers.name: net_ice_servers

net_ice_usewebrtc.description: Use webrtc's extra overheads rather than simple ICE. This makes packets larger and is slower to connect, but is compatible with the web port.
net_ice_usewebrtc.name: net_ice_usewebrtc

net_mtu.description: Specifies a maximum udp payload size, above which packets will be fragmented. If routers all worked properly this could be some massive value, and some massive value may work really nicely for lans. Use smaller values than the default if you're connecting through nested tunnels through routers that fail with IP fragmentation.
net_mtu.name: net_mtu

nosound.description: Disable all sound from the engine. Cannot be overriden by configs or anything if set via the -nosound commandline argument.
nosound.name: nosound

pext_ezquake_nochunks.description: Prevents ezquake clients from being able to use the chunked download extension. This sidesteps numerous ezquake issues, and will make downloads slower but more robust.
pext_ezquake_nochunks.name: pext_ezquake_nochunks

pext_ezquake_verfortrans.description: ezQuake does not implement PEXT_TRANS properly. This is the version of ezquake required for PEXT_TRANS to be allowed. This was still broken when I wrote this description, hence the large value.
pext_ezquake_verfortrans.name: pext_ezquake_verfortrans

pext_predinfo.description: Enables some extra things to support prediction over NQ protocols.
pext_predinfo.name: pext_predinfo

pext_replacementdeltas.description: Enables the use of alternative nack-based entity deltas
pext_replacementdeltas.name: pext_replacementdeltas

pkg_autoupdate.description:
Controls autoupdates, can only be changed via the downloads menu.
0: off.
1: enabled (stable only).
2: enabled (unstable).
Note that autoupdate will still prompt the user to actually apply the changes.
pkg_autoupdate.name: pkg_autoupdate

plug_loaddefault.description:
0: Load plugins only via explicit plug_load commands
1: Load built-in plugins and those selected via the package manager
2: Scan for misc plugins, loading all that can be found, but not built-ins.
3: Scan for plugins, and then load any built-ins
plug_loaddefault.name: plug_loaddefault

plug_sbar.description:
Controls whether plugins are allowed to draw the hud, rather than the engine (when allowed by csqc). This is typically used to permit the ezhud plugin without needing to bother unloading it.
=0: never use hud plugins.
&1: Use hud plugins in deathmatch.
&2: Use hud plugins in singleplayer/coop.
=3: Always use hud plugins (when loaded).
plug_sbar.name: plug_sbar

pm_airstep.description: Allows players to step up while jumping. This makes stairs more graceful but also increases potential jump heights.
pm_airstep.name: pm_airstep

pm_autobunny.description: Players will continue jumping without needing to release the jump button.
pm_autobunny.name: pm_autobunny

pm_bunnyfriction.description: Replicates NQ behaviour, ensuring that there's at least a frame of friction while jumping - friction is proportional to tick rate.
pm_bunnyfriction.name: pm_bunnyfriction

pm_bunnyspeedcap.description: 0 or 1, ish. If the player is traveling faster than this speed while turning, their velocity will be gracefully reduced to match their current maxspeed. You can still rocket-jump to gain high velocity, but turning will reduce your speed back to the max. This can be used to disable bunny hopping.
pm_bunnyspeedcap.name: pm_bunnyspeedcap

pm_edgefriction.description: Increases friction when about to walk over a cliff, so you're less likely to plummet by mistake. When empty defaults to 2, but uses a tracebox instead of a traceline to detect the drop.
pm_edgefriction.name: pm_edgefriction

pm_flyfriction.description: Amount of friction that applies in fly or 6dof mode. Empty means 4.
pm_flyfriction.name: pm_flyfriction

pm_noround.description: Disables player prediction snapping, in a way that cannot be reliably predicted but may be needed to avoid map bugs.
pm_noround.name: pm_noround

pm_pground.description: Use persisten onground state instead of recalculating every frame.Do NOT use with nq mods, as most nq mods will interfere with onground state, resulting in glitches.
pm_pground.name: pm_pground

pm_slidefix.description: Fixes an issue when walking down slopes (ie: so they act more like slopes and not a series of steps)
pm_slidefix.name: pm_slidefix

pm_slidyslopes.description: Replicates NQ behaviour, where players will slowly slide down ramps. Generally requires 'pm_noround 1' too, otherwise the effect rounds to nothing.
pm_slidyslopes.name: pm_slidyslopes

pm_stepdown.description: Causes physics to stick to the ground, instead of constantly losing traction while going down steps.
pm_stepdown.name: pm_stepdown

pm_stepheight.description: If empty, the value  will be used instead. This is the size of the step you can step up or down.
pm_stepheight.name: pm_stepheight

pm_walljump.description: Allows the player to bounce off walls while arborne.
pm_walljump.name: pm_walljump

pm_watersinkspeed.description: This is the speed that players will sink at while inactive in water. Empty means 60.
pm_watersinkspeed.name: pm_watersinkspeed

pr_allowbutton1.description: The button1 field is believed to have been intended to work with the +use command, but it was never hooked up. In NetQuake, this field was often repurposed for other things as it was not otherwise used (and cannot be removed without breaking the crc), while third-party QuakeWorld engines did decide to implement it as believed was intended. As a result, this cvar only applies to QuakeWorld mods and a value of 1 is only likely to cause issues with NQ mods that were ported to QW.
pr_allowbutton1.name: pr_allowbutton1

pr_autocreatecvars.description: Implicitly create any cvars that don't exist when read.
pr_autocreatecvars.name: pr_autocreatecvars

pr_compatabilitytest.description: Only enables builtins if the extension they are part of was queried.
pr_compatabilitytest.name: pr_compatabilitytest

pr_debugger.description: When enabled, QC errors and debug events will enable step-by-step tracing.
pr_debugger.name: pr_debugger

pr_droptofloorunits.description: Distance that droptofloor is allowed to drop to be considered successul.
pr_droptofloorunits.name: pr_droptofloorunits

pr_enable_profiling.description: Enables profiling support. Will run more slowly. Change the map and then use the profile_ssqc/profile_csqc commands to see the results.
pr_enable_profiling.name: pr_enable_profiling

pr_enable_uriget.description: Allows gamecode to make direct http requests
pr_enable_uriget.name: pr_enable_uriget

pr_engine.description: This cvar exists so that the menuqc is able to determine which engine-specific settings/values to list/suggest. It must not be used to detect formal QC extensions/builtins. Use checkextension/checkbuiltin/checkcommand for that.
pr_engine.name: pr_engine

pr_ext_dp_qc_getsurface.description: Set to 0 to block detection of the extension
pr_ext_dp_qc_getsurface.name: pr_ext_dp_qc_getsurface

pr_fixbrokenqccarrays.description:
As part of its nq/qw/h2/csqc support, FTE remaps QC fields to match an internal order. This is a faster way to handle extended fields. However, some QCCs are buggy and don't report all field defs.
0: do nothing. QCC must be well behaved.
1: Duplicate engine fields, remap the ones we can to known offsets. This is sufficient for QCCX/FrikQCC mods that use hardcoded or even occasional calculated offsets (fixes ktpro).
2: Scan the mod for field accessing instructions, and assume those are the fields (and that they don't alias non-fields). This can be used to work around gmqcc's WTFs (fixes xonotic).
pr_fixbrokenqccarrays.name: pr_fixbrokenqccarrays

pr_gc_threaded.description: Says whether to use a separate thread for tempstring garbage collections. This avoids main-thread stalls but at the expense of more memory usage.
pr_gc_threaded.name: pr_gc_threaded

pr_imitatemvdsv.description: Enables mvdsv-specific builtins, and fakes identifiers so that mods made for mvdsv can run properly and with the full feature set.
pr_imitatemvdsv.name: pr_imitatemvdsv

pr_maxedicts.description: Maximum number of entities spawnable on the map at once. Low values will crash the server on some maps/mods. High values will result in excessive memory useage (see pr_ssqc_memsize). Illegible server messages may occur with old/other clients above 32k. FTE's network protocols have a maximum at a little over 4 million. Please don't ever make a mod that actually uses that many...
pr_maxedicts.name: pr_maxedicts

pr_no_parsecommand.description: Provides a way around invalid mod usage of SV_ParseClientCommand, eg xonotic.
pr_no_parsecommand.name: pr_no_parsecommand

pr_no_playerphysics.description: Prevents support of the 'SV_PlayerPhysics' QC function. This allows servers to prevent needless breakage of player prediction.
pr_no_playerphysics.name: pr_no_playerphysics

pr_nonetaccess.description: Block all direct access to network buffers (the writebyte builtin and friends will ignore the call).
pr_nonetaccess.name: pr_nonetaccess

pr_precachepic_slow.description: Legacy setting. Should be set to 0 where supported.
pr_precachepic_slow.name: pr_precachepic_slow

pr_sourcedir.description: Subdirectory where your qc source is located. Used by the internal compiler and qc debugging functionality.
pr_sourcedir.name: pr_sourcedir

pr_ssqc_memsize.description: The ammount of memory available to the QC vm. This has a theoretical maximum of 1gb, but that value can only really be used in 64bit builds. -1 will attempt to use some conservative default, but you may need to increase it. Consider also clearing pr_fixbrokenqccarrays if you need to change this cvar.
pr_ssqc_memsize.name: pr_ssqc_memsize

pr_tempstringcount.description: Obsolete. Set to 16 if you want to recycle+reuse the same 16 tempstring references and break lots of mods.
pr_tempstringcount.name: pr_tempstringcount

q3bsp_ignorestyles.description: Ignores multiple lightstyles in Raven's q3bsp variant(and derivatives) for better batch/rendering performance.
q3bsp_ignorestyles.name: q3bsp_ignorestyles

q3bsp_mergelightmaps.description: Specifies whether to merge lightmaps into atlases in order to boost performance. Unfortunately this breaks tcgen on lightmap passes - if you care, set this to 0.
q3bsp_mergelightmaps.name: q3bsp_mergelightmaps

q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_flag.description: The surfaceparm flag(s) that enables q3bsp trisoup collision
q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_flag.name: q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_flag

q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_force.description: Force mesh-based collisions on all q3bsp trisoup surfaces.
q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_force.name: q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_force

qtv_maxstreams.description: This is the maximum number of QTV clients/proxies that may be directly connected to the server. If empty then there is no limit. 0 disallows any streaming.
qtv_maxstreams.name: qtv_maxstreams

r_bloom.description: Enables bloom (light bleeding from bright objects). Fractional values reduce the amount shown.
r_bloom.name: r_bloom

r_bloom_downsize.description: Technically more correct with a value of 1, but you probably won't notice.
r_bloom_downsize.name: r_bloom_downsize

r_bloom_filter.description: Controls how bright the image must get before it will bloom (3 separate values, in RGB order).
r_bloom_filter.name: r_bloom_filter

r_bloom_initialscale.description: Initial scaling factor for bloom. should be either 1 or 0.5
r_bloom_initialscale.name: r_bloom_initialscale

r_bloom_retain.description: How much of the regular scene to retain when bloom is active.
r_bloom_retain.name: r_bloom_retain

r_bloom_size.description: Target bloom kernel size (assuming a video width of 320).
r_bloom_size.name: r_bloom_size

r_bluelight_colour.description: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_BLUE effects (typically used for quad-damage in quakeworld)
r_bluelight_colour.name: r_bluelight_colour

r_bouncysparks.description: Enables particle interaction with world surfaces, allowing for bouncy particles, stains, and decals.
r_bouncysparks.name: r_bouncysparks

r_brightlight_colour.description: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_BRIGHTLIGHT effects (unused in vanilla quake).
r_brightlight_colour.name: r_brightlight_colour

r_clutter_density.description: Scaler for clutter counts. 0 disables clutter completely.\nClutter requires shaders with 'fte_clutter MODEL SPACING SCALEMIN SCALEMAX ZOFS ANGLEMIN ANGLEMAX' terms
r_clutter_density.name: r_clutter_density

r_clutter_distance.description: Distance at which clutter will become invisible.
r_clutter_distance.name: r_clutter_distance

r_coronas.description: Draw coronas on realtime lights. Overrides glquake-esque flashblends.
r_coronas.name: r_coronas

r_coronas_fadedist.description: Coronas will fade out over this distance.
r_coronas_fadedist.name: r_coronas_fadedist

r_coronas_mindist.description: Coronas closer than this will be invisible, preventing near clip plane issues.
r_coronas_mindist.name: r_coronas_mindist

r_coronas_occlusion.description:
Specifies that coronas should be occluded more carefully.
0: No occlusion, at all.
1: BSP occlusion only (simple tracelines).
2: non-bsp occlusion also (complex tracelines).
3: Depthbuffer reads (forces synchronisation).
4: occlusion queries.
r_coronas_occlusion.name: r_coronas_occlusion

r_decal_noperpendicular.description: When enabled, decals will not be generated on planes at a steep angle from clipped decal orientation.
r_decal_noperpendicular.name: r_decal_noperpendicular

r_deluxemapping.description:
Enables bumpmapping based upon precomputed light directions.
0=off
1=use if available
2=auto-generate (if possible)
r_deluxemapping.name: r_deluxemapping

r_dimlight_colour.description: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_DIMLIGHT effects (used for quad+pent in vanilla quake).
r_dimlight_colour.name: r_dimlight_colour

r_dodgymiptex.description: When enabled, this will force regeneration of mipmaps, discarding mips1-4 like glquake did. This may eg solve fullbright issues with some maps, but may reduce distant detail levels.
r_dodgymiptex.name: r_dodgymiptex

r_dodgypcxfiles.description: When enabled, this will ignore the palette stored within pcx files, for compatibility with quake2.
r_dodgypcxfiles.name: r_dodgypcxfiles

r_dodgytgafiles.description: Many old glquake engines had a buggy tga loader that ignored bottom-up flags. Naturally people worked around this and the world was plagued with buggy images. Most engines have now fixed the bug, but you can reenable it if you have bugged tga files.
r_dodgytgafiles.name: r_dodgytgafiles

r_drawentities.description:
Controls whether to draw entities or not.
0: Draw no entities.
1: Draw everything as normal.
2: Draw everything but bmodels.
3: Draw bmodels only.
r_drawentities.name: r_drawentities

r_drawflame.description: Set to -1 to disable ALL static entities. Set to 0 to disable only wall torches and standing flame. Set to 1 for everything drawn as normal.
r_drawflame.name: r_drawflame

r_dynamic.description: 0: no standard dlights at all.\n1: coloured dlights will be used, they may show through walls. These are not realtime things.\n2: The dlights will be forced to monochrome (this does not affect coronas/flashblends/rtlights attached to the same light).
r_dynamic.name: r_dynamic

r_editlights.description: enables .rtlights file editing mode. Consider using csaddon/equivelent instead.
r_editlights.name: r_editlights

r_editlights_cursordistance.description: maximum distance of cursor from eye
r_editlights_cursordistance.name: r_editlights_cursordistance

r_editlights_cursorgrid.description: snaps cursor to this grid size
r_editlights_cursorgrid.name: r_editlights_cursorgrid

r_editlights_cursorpushback.description: how far to pull the cursor back toward the eye, for some reason
r_editlights_cursorpushback.name: r_editlights_cursorpushback

r_editlights_cursorpushoff.description: how far to push the cursor off the impacted surface
r_editlights_cursorpushoff.name: r_editlights_cursorpushoff

r_editlights_import_ambient.description: ambient light scaler for imported lights
r_editlights_import_ambient.name: r_editlights_import_ambient

r_editlights_import_diffuse.description: diffuse light scaler for imported lights
r_editlights_import_diffuse.name: r_editlights_import_diffuse

r_editlights_import_radius.description: changes size of light entities loaded from a map
r_editlights_import_radius.name: r_editlights_import_radius

r_editlights_import_specular.description: specular light scaler for imported lights
r_editlights_import_specular.name: r_editlights_import_specular

r_explosionlight_colour.description: This controls the initial RGB values of EF_EXPLOSION effects.
r_explosionlight_colour.name: r_explosionlight_colour

r_explosionlight_fade.description: This controls the per-second RGB decay values of EF_EXPLOSION effects.
r_explosionlight_fade.name: r_explosionlight_fade

r_fastturbcolour.description: The colour to use for water surfaces draw with r_waterstyle 0.
r_fastturbcolour.name: r_fastturbcolour

r_fb_bmodels.description: Enables loading lumas on the map, as well as any external bsp models.
r_fb_bmodels.name: r_fb_bmodels

r_fb_models.description: Enables the use of lumas on models. Note that if ruleset_allow_fbmodels is enabled, then all models are unconditionally fullbright in deathmatch, because cheaters would set up their models like that anyway, hurrah for beating them at their own game. QuakeWorld players suck.
r_fb_models.name: r_fb_models

r_fog_cullentities.description: 0: Never cull entities by fog...\n1: Automatically cull entities according to fog.\n2: Force fog culling regardless
r_fog_cullentities.name: r_fog_cullentities

r_fog_exp2.description: Expresses how fog fades with distance. 0 (matching DarkPlaces's default) is typically more realistic, while 1 (matching FitzQuake and others) is more common.
r_fog_exp2.name: r_fog_exp2

r_fog_linear.description: 0: Use Exp/Exp2 fog. 1: Use linear fog.
