r_fog_linear.name: r_fog_linear

r_fog_permutation.description: Renders fog using a material permutation. 0 plays nicer with q3 shaders, but 1 is otherwise a better choice.
r_fog_permutation.name: r_fog_permutation

r_font_postprocess_outline.description: Controls the number of pixels of dark borders to use around fonts.
r_font_postprocess_outline.name: r_font_postprocess_outline

r_forceprogramify.description: Reduce the shader to a single texture, and then make stuff up about its mother. The resulting fist fight results in more colour when you shine a light upon its face.\nSet to 2 to ignore 'depthfunc equal' and 'tcmod scale' in order to tolerate bizzare shaders made for a bizzare engine.\nBecause most shaders made for DP are by people who _clearly_ have no idea what the heck they're doing, you'll typically need the '2' setting.
r_forceprogramify.name: r_forceprogramify

r_fullbright.description: Ignore world lightmaps, drawing *everything* fully lit.
r_fullbright.name: r_fullbright

r_fullbrightSkins.description: Force the use of fullbright skins on other players. No more hiding in the dark.
r_fullbrightSkins.name: r_fullbrightSkins

r_fxaa.description: Runs a post-procesing pass to strip the jaggies.
r_fxaa.name: r_fxaa

r_globalskin_count.description: Specifies how many globalskins there are.
r_globalskin_count.name: r_globalskin_count

r_globalskin_first.description: Specifies the first .skin value that is a global skin. Entities within this range will use the shader/image called 'gfx/skinSKIN.lmp' instead of their regular skin. See also: r_globalskin_count.
r_globalskin_first.name: r_globalskin_first

r_glsl_emissive.description: When set, specifies that the _luma or _glow textures are emissive... When 0 they are taken as a mask for the proportion of the lightmap that will apply (for q2e compat, has issues with overbrights).
r_glsl_emissive.name: r_glsl_emissive

r_glsl_offsetmapping.description: Enables the use of paralax mapping, adding fake depth to textures.
r_glsl_offsetmapping.name: r_glsl_offsetmapping

r_glsl_offsetmapping_reliefmapping.description: Changes the paralax sampling mode to be a bit nicer, but noticably more expensive at high resolutions. r_glsl_offsetmapping must be set.
r_glsl_offsetmapping_reliefmapping.name: r_glsl_offsetmapping_reliefmapping

r_glsl_precache.description: Force all relevant glsl permutations to load upfront.
r_glsl_precache.name: r_glsl_precache

r_glsl_skybox_autorotate.description: Defines the axis around which skyboxes will rotate (the first three values). The fourth value defines the speed the skybox rotates at, in degrees per second.
r_glsl_skybox_autorotate.name: r_glsl_skybox_autorotate

r_glsl_skybox_orientation.description: Defines the axis around which skyboxes will rotate (the first three values). The fourth value defines the speed the skybox rotates at, in degrees per second.
r_glsl_skybox_orientation.name: r_glsl_skybox_orientation

r_glsl_turbscale_reflect.description: Controls the strength of the water reflection ripples (used by the altwater glsl code).
r_glsl_turbscale_reflect.name: r_glsl_turbscale_reflect

r_glsl_turbscale_refract.description: Controls the strength of the underwater ripples (used by the altwater glsl code).
r_glsl_turbscale_refract.name: r_glsl_turbscale_refract

r_graphics.description: Turning this off will result in ascii-style rendering.
r_graphics.name: r_graphics

r_greenlight_colour.description: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_GREEN effects (rarely used).
r_greenlight_colour.name: r_greenlight_colour

r_halfrate.description: Use half-rate shading (where supported by gpu).
r_halfrate.name: r_halfrate

r_hdr_framebuffer.description: If enabled, the map will be rendered into a high-precision image framebuffer. This avoids issues with shaders that contribute more than 1 in any single pass (like overbrights). Can also be set to the name of an image format, to force rendering to that format first - interesting formats are L8, RGB565, B10G11R11F, and others.
r_hdr_framebuffer.name: r_hdr_framebuffer

r_ignoreentpvs.description: Disables pvs culling of entities that have been submitted to the renderer.
r_ignoreentpvs.name: r_ignoreentpvs

r_ignoremapprefixes.description: Ignores when textures were loaded from map-specific paths.\n0: textures/foo/tex.tga will not be confused with textures/foo/tex.tga.\n1: The same texture might be loaded multiple times over.
r_ignoremapprefixes.name: r_ignoremapprefixes

r_image_downloadsizelimit.description: The maximum allowed file size of images loaded from a web-based url. 0 disables completely, while empty imposes no limit.
r_image_downloadsizelimit.name: r_image_downloadsizelimit

r_imageextensions.description: The list of image file extensions which might exist on disk (note that this does not list all supported formats, only the extensions that should be searched for).
r_imageextensions.name: r_imageextensions

r_keepimages.description: Retain unused images in memory for slightly faster map loading.\n0: Redundant images will be purged after each map change.\n1: Images will be retained until vid_reload (potentially consuming a lot of ram).
r_keepimages.name: r_keepimages

r_lavastyle.description: See r_waterstyle, but affects only lava. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.
r_lavastyle.name: r_lavastyle

r_lightmap_format.description: Overrides the default texture format used for lightmaps. rgb9e5 is a good choice for HDR.
r_lightmap_format.name: r_lightmap_format

r_lightprepass.description: Experimental. Attempt to use a different lighting mechanism (aka: deferred lighting). Requires vid_reload to take effect.
r_lightprepass.name: r_lightprepass

r_loadlit.description:
Whether to load lit files.
0: Do not load external rgb lightmap data.
1: Load but don't generate.
2: Generate ldr lighting (if none found).
3: Generate hdr lighting (if none found).
Note that regeneration of lightmap data may be unreliable if the map was made for more advanced lighting tools.
Deluxemap information will also be generated, as appropriate.
r_loadlit.name: r_loadlit

r_loadsurfenvmaps.description: Load local reflection environment-maps, where available. These are normally defined via env_cubemap entities dotted around the place.
r_loadsurfenvmaps.name: r_loadsurfenvmaps

r_lodbias.description: Biases the level-of-detail on models (for those that have lod).
r_lodbias.name: r_lodbias

r_lodscale.description: Scales the level-of-detail reduction on models (for those that have lod).
r_lodscale.name: r_lodscale

r_max_gpu_bones.description: Specifies the maximum number of bones that can be handled on the GPU. If empty, will guess.
r_max_gpu_bones.name: r_max_gpu_bones

r_meshpitch.description: Specifies the direction of the pitch angle on mesh models formats, Quake compatibility requires -1.
r_meshpitch.name: r_meshpitch

r_meshroll.description: Specifies the direction of the roll angle on mesh models formats, also affects gamecode, so do not change from its default.
r_meshroll.name: r_meshroll

r_mirroralpha.description: Specifies how the default shader is generated for the 'window02_1' texture. Values less than 1 will turn it into a mirror.
r_mirroralpha.name: r_mirroralpha

r_muzzleflash_colour.description: This controls the initial RGB+radius of EF_MUZZLEFLASH/svc_muzzleflash effects.
r_muzzleflash_colour.name: r_muzzleflash_colour

r_muzzleflash_fade.description: This controls the per-second RGB+radius decay of EF_MUZZLEFLASH/svc_muzzleflash effects.
r_muzzleflash_fade.name: r_muzzleflash_fade

r_netgraph.description: Displays a graph of packet latency. A value of 2 will give additional info about what sort of data is being received from the server.
r_netgraph.name: r_netgraph

r_nolerp_list.description: Models in this list will not interpolate. Any models included here should be considered bad.
r_nolerp_list.name: r_nolerp_list

r_noshadow_list.description: Models in this list will not cast shadows.
r_noshadow_list.name: r_noshadow_list

r_part_classic_expgrav.description: Scaler for how fast classic explosion particles should accelerate due to gravity. 1 for like vanilla, 10 for like zquake.
r_part_classic_expgrav.name: r_part_classic_expgrav

r_part_classic_opaque.description: Disables transparency on classic particles, for the oldskool look.
r_part_classic_opaque.name: r_part_classic_opaque

r_part_classic_square.description: Enables square particles, for the oldskool look.
r_part_classic_square.name: r_part_classic_square

r_part_contentswitch.description: Enable particle effects to change based on content (ex. water).
r_part_contentswitch.name: r_part_contentswitch

r_part_rain.description: Enable particle effects to emit off of surfaces. Mainly used for weather or lava/slime effects.
r_part_rain.name: r_part_rain

r_particle_tracelimit.description: Number of traces to allow per frame for particle physics.
r_particle_tracelimit.name: r_particle_tracelimit

r_polygonoffset_submodel_factor.description: z-fighting avoidance. Pushes submodel depth values slightly towards the camera depending on the slope of the surface.
r_polygonoffset_submodel_factor.name: r_polygonoffset_submodel_factor

r_polygonoffset_submodel_map.description: List of maps on which z-fighting reduction should be used. wildcards accepted.
r_polygonoffset_submodel_map.name: r_polygonoffset_submodel_map

r_polygonoffset_submodel_offset.description: z-fighting avoidance. Pushes submodel depth values slightly towards the camera by a consistent distance.
r_polygonoffset_submodel_offset.name: r_polygonoffset_submodel_offset

r_portaldrawplanes.description: Draw front and back planes in portals. Debug feature.
r_portaldrawplanes.name: r_portaldrawplanes

r_portalonly.description: Don't draw things which are not portals. Debug feature.
r_portalonly.name: r_portalonly

r_portalrecursion.description: The number of portals the camera is allowed to recurse through.
r_portalrecursion.name: r_portalrecursion

r_postprocshader.description: Specifies a custom shader to use as a post-processing shader
r_postprocshader.name: r_postprocshader

r_projection.description:
0: regular perspective.
1: stereographic.
2: fisheye.
3: panoramic.
4: lambert azimuthal equal-area.
5: equirectangular.
6: panini.
r_projection.name: r_projection

r_redlight_colour.description: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_RED effects (typically used for pentagram in quakeworld).
r_redlight_colour.name: r_redlight_colour

r_refract_fbo.description: Use an fbo for refraction. If 0, just renders as a portal and uses a copy of the current framebuffer.
r_refract_fbo.name: r_refract_fbo

r_refractreflect_scale.description: Use a different scale for refraction and reflection texturemaps. Because $reasons.
r_refractreflect_scale.name: r_refractreflect_scale

r_renderscale.description: Provides a way to enable subsampling or super-sampling
r_renderscale.name: r_renderscale

r_replacemodels.description: A list of filename extensions to attempt to use instead of mdl.
r_replacemodels.name: r_replacemodels

r_rocketlight_colour.description: This controls the RGB+radius values of MF_ROCKET effects.
r_rocketlight_colour.name: r_rocketlight_colour

r_shaderblobs.description: If enabled, can massively accelerate vid restarts / loading (especially with the d3d renderer). Can cause issues when upgrading engine versions, so this is disabled by default.
r_shaderblobs.name: r_shaderblobs

r_shadow_bumpscale_basetexture.description: bumpyness scaler for generation of fallback normalmap textures from models
r_shadow_bumpscale_basetexture.name: r_shadow_bumpscale_basetexture

r_shadow_heightscale_basetexture.description: scaler for generation of height maps from legacy paletted content.
r_shadow_heightscale_basetexture.name: r_shadow_heightscale_basetexture

r_shadow_playershadows.description: Controls the presence of shadows on the local player.
r_shadow_playershadows.name: r_shadow_playershadows

r_shadow_raytrace.description: Enables use of hardware raytracing for shadows. Consider also using with r_halfrate.
r_shadow_raytrace.name: r_shadow_raytrace

r_shadow_realtime_dlight.description: Enables the use of dynamic realtime lights, allowing explosions to use bumpmaps etc properly.
r_shadow_realtime_dlight.name: r_shadow_realtime_dlight

r_shadow_realtime_dlight_shadows.description: Allows dynamic realtime lights to cast shadows as they move.
r_shadow_realtime_dlight_shadows.name: r_shadow_realtime_dlight_shadows

r_shadow_realtime_nonworld_lightmaps.description: Scaler for lightmaps used when not using realtime world lighting. Probably broken.
r_shadow_realtime_nonworld_lightmaps.name: r_shadow_realtime_nonworld_lightmaps

r_shadow_realtime_world.description: Enables the use of static/world realtime lights.
r_shadow_realtime_world.name: r_shadow_realtime_world

r_shadow_realtime_world_importlightentit.description:
Controls default loading of map-based realtime lights.
0: Load explicit .rtlight files only.
1: Load explicit lights then try fallback to parsing the entities lump.
2: Load only the entities lump.
r_shadow_realtime_world_importlightentit.name: r_shadow_realtime_world_importlightentitiesfrommap

r_shadow_realtime_world_lightmaps.description: Specifies how much of the map's normal lightmap to retain when using world realtime lights. 0 completely replaces lighting.
r_shadow_realtime_world_lightmaps.name: r_shadow_realtime_world_lightmaps

r_shadow_scissor.description: constrains stencil shadows to the onscreen box that contains the maxmium extents of the light. This avoids unnecessary work.
r_shadow_scissor.name: r_shadow_scissor

r_shadow_shadowmapping.description: Enables soft shadows instead of stencil shadows.
r_shadow_shadowmapping.name: r_shadow_shadowmapping

r_shadow_shadowmapping_precision.description: Scales the shadowmap detail level up or down.
r_shadow_shadowmapping_precision.name: r_shadow_shadowmapping_precision

r_shadows.description: Draw basic blob shadows underneath entities without using realtime lighting.
r_shadows.name: r_shadows

r_shadows_fakedistance.description: The radius to use for fake shadows.
r_shadows_fakedistance.name: r_shadows_fakedistance

r_shadows_focus.description: Offset for the center of the fake-shadows volume.
r_shadows_focus.name: r_shadows_focus

r_shadows_throwdirection.description: The direction to throw the fake shadows in. Should ideally be opposite to r_sun_dir, but that just shows how fake these things actually are.
r_shadows_throwdirection.name: r_shadows_throwdirection

r_showbboxes.description: Debugging. Shows bounding boxes. 1=ssqc, 2=csqc. Red=solid, Green=stepping/toss/bounce, Blue=onground.
r_showbboxes.name: r_showbboxes

r_showfields.description: Debugging. Shows entity fields boxes (entity closest to crosshair). 1=ssqc, 2=csqc, 3=snapshots.
r_showfields.name: r_showfields

r_showshaders.description: Debugging. Shows the name of the (worldmodel) shader being pointed to.
r_showshaders.name: r_showshaders

r_showtris.description: Developer feature where everything is drawn with wireframe over the top. Only active where cheats are permitted.
r_showtris.name: r_showtris

r_skycloudalpha.description: Controls how opaque the front layer of legacy scrolling skies should be.
r_skycloudalpha.name: r_skycloudalpha

r_skyfog.description: This controls an alpha-blend value for fog on skyboxes, cumulative with regular fog alpha.
r_skyfog.name: r_skyfog

r_slimestyle.description: See r_waterstyle, but affects only slime. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.
r_slimestyle.name: r_slimestyle

r_softwarebanding.description: Utilise the Quake colormap in order to emulate 8bit software rendering. This results in banding as well as other artifacts that some believe adds character. Also forces nearest sampling on affected surfaces (palette indicies do not interpolate well).
r_softwarebanding.name: r_softwarebanding

r_sprite_backfacing.description: Make oriented sprites face backwards relative to their orientation, for compat with q1.
r_sprite_backfacing.name: r_sprite_backfacing

r_stereo_convergence.description: Nudges the angle of each eye inwards when using stereoscopic rendering.
r_stereo_convergence.name: r_stereo_convergence

r_stereo_method.description:
Value 0 = Off.
Value 1 = Attempt hardware acceleration. Requires vid_restart.
Value 2 = red/cyan.
Value 3 = red/blue.
Value 4=red/green.
Value 5=eye strain.
r_stereo_method.name: r_stereo_method

r_stereo_separation.description: How far apart your eyes are, in quake units. A non-zero value will enable stereoscoping rendering. You might need some of them retro 3d glasses. Hardware support is recommended, see r_stereo_context.
r_stereo_separation.name: r_stereo_separation

r_sun_colour.description: Specifies the colour of sunlight that appears in the form of crepuscular rays.
r_sun_colour.name: r_sun_colour

r_sun_dir.description: Specifies the direction that crepusular rays appear along
r_sun_dir.name: r_sun_dir

r_telestyle.description: See r_waterstyle, but affects only teleporters. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.
r_telestyle.name: r_telestyle

r_temporalscenecache.description: Controls whether to generate+reuse a scene cache over multiple frames. This is generated on a separate thread to avoid any associated costs. This can significantly boost framerates on complex maps, but can also stress the gpu more (performance tradeoff that varies per map). An outdated cache may be used if the cache takes too long to build (eg: lightmap animations), which could cause the odd glitch when moving fast (but retain more consistent framerates - another tradeoff).\n0: Tranditional quake rendering.\n1: Generate+Use the scene cache.
r_temporalscenecache.name: r_temporalscenecache

r_tessellation.description: Enables+controls the use of blinn tessellation on the fallback shader for meshes, equivelent to a shader with 'program defaultskin#TESS'. This will look stupid unless the meshes were actually designed for it and have suitable vertex normals.
r_tessellation.name: r_tessellation

r_torch.description: Generate a dynamic light at the player's position.
r_torch.name: r_torch

r_tracker_fadetime.description: how long it takes for r_tracker messages to fully fade once they start fading\n
r_tracker_fadetime.name: r_tracker_fadetime

r_tracker_frags.description:
0: like vanilla quake
1: shows only your kills/deaths
2: shows all kills
r_tracker_frags.name: r_tracker_frags

r_tracker_lines.description: number of r_tracker messages to display\n
r_tracker_lines.name: r_tracker_lines

r_tracker_time.description: how long it takes for r_tracker messages to start fading\n
r_tracker_time.name: r_tracker_time

r_tracker_w.description: width of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's width, eg 0.5\n
r_tracker_w.name: r_tracker_w

r_tracker_x.description: left position of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's width, eg 0.5\n
r_tracker_x.name: r_tracker_x

r_tracker_y.description: top position of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's height, eg 0.333\n
r_tracker_y.name: r_tracker_y

r_vertexdlights.description: Determine model lighting with respect to nearby dlights. Poor-man's rtlights.
r_vertexdlights.name: r_vertexdlights

r_vertexlight.description: Hack loaded shaders to remove detail pass and lightmap sampling for faster rendering.
r_vertexlight.name: r_vertexlight

r_viewmodel_fov.description: field of vision, 1-170 degrees, standard fov is 90, nquake defaults to 108.
r_viewmodel_fov.name: r_viewmodel_fov

r_viewmodel_quake.description: Controls whether to use weird viewmodel movements from vanilla quake.
r_viewmodel_quake.name: r_viewmodel_quake

r_viewpreselgun.description: HACK: Display the preselected weaponmodel, instead of the current weaponmodel.
r_viewpreselgun.name: r_viewpreselgun

r_waterstyle.description:
Changes how water, and teleporters are drawn. Possible values are:
0: fastturb-style block colour.
1: regular q1-style water.
2: refraction(ripply and transparent)
3: refraction with reflection at an angle
4: ripplemapped without reflections (requires particle effects)
5: ripples+reflections
r_waterstyle.name: r_waterstyle

r_waterwarp.description: Enables fullscreen warp, preferably via glsl. -1 specifies to force the fov warp fallback instead which can give a smidge more performance.
r_waterwarp.name: r_waterwarp

rank_autoadd.description: Automatically register players into the ranking system
rank_autoadd.name: rank_autoadd

rank_filename.description: Specifies which file to use as a rankings database. Enables the ranking system if set.
rank_filename.name: rank_filename

rank_needlogin.description: If set to 1, prohibits players from joining if they're not yet registered. This will require an external mechanism to register users, presumably via rcon.
rank_needlogin.name: rank_needlogin

rank_parms_last.description: Mod setting: the index of the last parm to be saved. Clamped to 32.
rank_parms_last.name: rank_parms_last

rate.description: A rough measure of the bandwidth to try to use while playing. Too high a value may result in 'buffer bloat'.
rate.name: rate

record_flush.description: If set, explicitly flushes demo data to disk while recording. This may be inefficient, depending on how your operating system is configured.
record_flush.name: record_flush

registered.description: Set if quake's pak1.pak is available
registered.name: registered

ruleset.description: Known rulesets are:\nnone: no explicit rules, all 'minor cheats' are allowed.\nstrict: equivelent to the smackdown ruleset. Note that this will block certain graphical enhancements too.
ruleset.name: ruleset

ruleset_allow_fbmodels.description: When 1, allows all models to be displayed fullbright, completely ignoring the lightmaps. This feature exists only for parity with ezquake's defaults.
ruleset_allow_fbmodels.name: ruleset_allow_fbmodels

ruleset_allow_frj.description: Specifies whether Forward-Rocket-Jump scripts are allowed in the current ruleset. If 0, limits on yaw speed will be imposed so they cannot be scripted.
ruleset_allow_frj.name: ruleset_allow_frj

ruleset_allow_larger_models.description: Enforces a maximum bounds limit on models, to prevent the use of additional spikes attached to the model from being used as a kind of wallhack.
ruleset_allow_larger_models.name: ruleset_allow_larger_models

ruleset_allow_localvolume.description: Allows the use of the snd_playersoundvolume cvar. Muting your own sounds can make it easier to hear where your opponent is.
ruleset_allow_localvolume.name: ruleset_allow_localvolume

ruleset_allow_modified_eyes.description: When 0, completely hides progs/eyes.mdl if it is not strictly identical to vanilla quake.
ruleset_allow_modified_eyes.name: ruleset_allow_modified_eyes

ruleset_allow_overlong_sounds.description: A setting of 0 will block the use of extra-long pickup sounds as item respawn timers.
ruleset_allow_overlong_sounds.name: ruleset_allow_overlong_sounds

ruleset_allow_packet.description: If 0, network packets sent via the 'packet' command will be blocked. This makes scripting timers a little harder.
ruleset_allow_packet.name: ruleset_allow_packet

ruleset_allow_particle_lightning.description: A setting of 0 blocks using the particle system to replace lightning gun trails. This prevents making the trails thinner thus preventing them from obscuring your view of your enemies.
ruleset_allow_particle_lightning.name: ruleset_allow_particle_lightning

ruleset_allow_playercount.description: Specifies whether teamplay triggers that count nearby players are allowed in the current ruleset.
ruleset_allow_playercount.name: ruleset_allow_playercount

ruleset_allow_semicheats.description: If 0, this blocks a range of cvars that are marked as semi-cheats. Such cvars will be locked to their empty/0 value.
ruleset_allow_semicheats.name: ruleset_allow_semicheats

ruleset_allow_sensitive_texture_replacem.description: Allows the replacement of certain model textures (as well as the models themselves). This prevents adding extra fullbrights to make them blatently obvious.
ruleset_allow_sensitive_texture_replacem.name: ruleset_allow_sensitive_texture_replacements

ruleset_allow_shaders.description: When 0, this completely disables the use of external shader files, preventing custom shaders from being used for wallhacks.
ruleset_allow_shaders.name: ruleset_allow_shaders

ruleset_allow_triggers.description: When 0, blocks the use of msg_trigger checks.
ruleset_allow_triggers.name: ruleset_allow_triggers

ruleset_allow_watervis.description: When 0, this enforces ugly opaque water.
ruleset_allow_watervis.name: ruleset_allow_watervis

s_al_debug.description: Enables periodic checks for OpenAL errors.
s_al_debug.name: s_al_debug

s_al_disable.description:
0: OpenAL works (generally as the highest priority).
1: OpenAL will be used only when a specific device is selected.
2: Don't allow ANY use of OpenAl.
With OpenAL disabled, audio ouput will fall back to platform-specific output, avoiding miscilaneous third-party openal limitation bugs.
s_al_disable.name: s_al_disable

s_al_distancemodel.description:
Controls how sounds fade with distance.
0: Inverse (most realistic)
1: Inverse Clamped
2: Linear (Quake-like)
3: Linear Clamped
4: Exponential
5: Exponential Clamped
6: None
s_al_distancemodel.name: s_al_distancemodel

s_al_dopplerfactor.description: Multiplies the strength of doppler effects.
s_al_dopplerfactor.name: s_al_dopplerfactor

s_al_hrtf.description:
Enables use of HRTF, and which HRTF table to use.
empty: auto, depending on openal config to enable it.
\0: force off.
1: Use the default HRTF.
s_al_hrtf.name: s_al_hrtf

s_al_reference_distance.description: This is the distance at which the sound is audiable with standard volume in the inverse distance models. Nearer sounds will be louder than the original sample.
s_al_reference_distance.name: s_al_reference_distance

s_al_speedofsound.description: Configures the speed of sound, in game units per second. This affects doppler.
s_al_speedofsound.name: s_al_speedofsound

s_al_use_reverb.description: Controls whether reverb effects will be used. Set to 0 to block them. Reverb requires gamecode to configure the reverb properties, other than underwater.
s_al_use_reverb.name: s_al_use_reverb

s_al_velocityscale.description: Rescales velocity values, before doppler can be calculated.
s_al_velocityscale.name: s_al_velocityscale

s_ambientlevel.description: This controls the volume levels of automatic area-based sounds (like water or sky), and is quite annoying. If you're playing deathmatch you'll definitely want this OFF.
s_ambientlevel.name: s_ambientlevel

s_device.description: This is the sound device(s) to use, in the form of driver:device.\nIf desired, multiple devices can be listed in space-seperated (quoted) tokens. _s_device_opts contains any enumerated options.\nIn all seriousness, use the menu to set this if you wish to keep your hair.
s_device.name: s_device

s_doppler.description: Enables doppler, with a multiplier for the scale.
s_doppler.name: s_doppler

s_doppler_max.description: Highest allowed doppler scale, to avoid things getting too weird.
s_doppler_max.name: s_doppler_max

s_inactive.description: Play sound while application is inactive (ie: tabbed out). Needs a snd_restart if changed.
s_inactive.name: s_inactive

s_khz.description: Sound speed, in kilohertz. Common values are 11, 22, 44, 48. Values above 1000 are explicitly in hertz.
s_khz.name: s_khz

s_loadas8bit.description: Downsample sounds on load as lower quality 8-bit sound, to save memory.
s_loadas8bit.name: s_loadas8bit

s_localvolume.description: Sound level for sounds local or originating from the player such as firing and pain sounds.
s_localvolume.name: s_localvolume

s_mixahead.description: Specifies how many seconds to prebuffer audio. Lower values give less latency, but might result in crackling. Different hardware/drivers have different tolerances, and this setting may be ignored completely where drivers are expected to provide their own tolerances.
s_mixahead.name: s_mixahead

s_mixerthread.description: When enabled sound mixing will be run on a separate thread. Currently supported only by directsound. Other drivers may unconditionally thread audio. Set to 0 only if you have issues.
s_mixerthread.name: s_mixerthread

s_nominaldistance.description: This cvar defines how far an attenuation=1 sound can be heard.
s_nominaldistance.name: s_nominaldistance

s_numspeakers.description: Number of hardware audio channels to use.  supports up to 6.
s_numspeakers.name: s_numspeakers

sbar_teamstatus.description: Display the last team say from each of your team members just above the sbar area.
sbar_teamstatus.name: sbar_teamstatus

scr_allowsnap.description: Whether to allow server-requested screenshot requests to check for gpu driver hacks.
scr_allowsnap.name: scr_allowsnap

scr_autoid.description: Display nametags above all players while spectating.
scr_autoid.name: scr_autoid

scr_autoid_armor.description: Display armour as part of nametags (when known).
scr_autoid_armor.name: scr_autoid_armor

scr_autoid_enemycolour.description: The colour for the text on the nametags of non-team members.
scr_autoid_enemycolour.name: scr_autoid_enemycolour

scr_autoid_health.description: Display health as part of nametags (when known).
scr_autoid_health.name: scr_autoid_health

scr_autoid_team.description: Display nametags above team members. 0: off. 1: display with half-alpha if occluded. 2: hide when occluded.
scr_autoid_team.name: scr_autoid_team

scr_autoid_teamcolour.description: The colour for the text on the nametags of team members.
scr_autoid_teamcolour.name: scr_autoid_teamcolour

scr_autoid_weapon.description: Display the player's best weapon as part of their nametag (when known).
scr_autoid_weapon.name: scr_autoid_weapon

scr_autoid_weapon_mask.description:
Mask of bits for weapon icons to actually show.
+1: Shotgun.
+2: Super Shotgun.
+4: Nail Gun.
+8: Super Nail Gun.
+16: Grenade Launcher.
+32: Rocket Launcher.
+64: Lightning
Showing only RL and GL is 96
scr_autoid_weapon_mask.name: scr_autoid_weapon_mask

scr_centertime.description: Centerprint messages will be displayed for this long before disappearing.
scr_centertime.name: scr_centertime

scr_conalpha.description: How opaque the console should be when there's still stuff going on behind.
scr_conalpha.name: scr_conalpha

scr_consize.description: Proportion of the screen to be covered by the console when its focused. Valid range is 0ish to 1.
scr_consize.name: scr_consize

scr_conspeed.description: How fast the console careers onto the screen.
scr_conspeed.name: scr_conspeed

scr_fov_mode.description:
Controls what the fov cvar actually controls:
0: largest axis (ultra-wide monitors means less height will be visible).
1: smallest axis (ultra-wide monitors will distort at the edges).
2: horizontal axis.
3: vertical axis.
4: 4:3 horizontal axis, padded for wider resolutions (for a more classic fov)
scr_fov_mode.name: scr_fov_mode

scr_loadingrefresh.description: Force redrawing of the loading screen, in order to display EVERY resource that is loaded
scr_loadingrefresh.name: scr_loadingrefresh

scr_loadingscreen_aspect.description:
Controls the aspect of levelshot images.
0: Use source image's aspect.
1: Force 4:3 aspect (ignore image's aspect), for best q3 compat.
2: Ignore aspect considerations and just smear it over the entire screen.
-1: Disable levelshot use.
scr_loadingscreen_aspect.name: scr_loadingscreen_aspect

scr_printspeed.description: How rapidly each character is displayed during outro messages.
scr_printspeed.name: scr_printspeed

scr_scoreboard_afk.description: Show 'afk' in the packetloss column when they're afk.
scr_scoreboard_afk.name: scr_scoreboard_afk

scr_scoreboard_backgroundalpha.description: Further multiplier for the background alphas.
scr_scoreboard_backgroundalpha.name: scr_scoreboard_backgroundalpha

scr_scoreboard_drawtitle.description: Wastes screen space when looking at the scoreboard.
scr_scoreboard_drawtitle.name: scr_scoreboard_drawtitle

scr_scoreboard_forcecolors.description: Makes the scoreboard colours obey enemycolor/teamcolor rules.
scr_scoreboard_forcecolors.name: scr_scoreboard_forcecolors

scr_scoreboard_newstyle.description: Display team colours and stuff in a style popularised by Electro. Looks more modern, but might not quite fit classic huds.
scr_scoreboard_newstyle.name: scr_scoreboard_newstyle

scr_scoreboard_ping_status.description: Threshholds required to switch ping display from green to white, yellow, megenta and red.
scr_scoreboard_ping_status.name: scr_scoreboard_ping_status

scr_scoreboard_showflags.description:
Display flag caps+touches on the scoreboard, where our fragfile.dat supports them.
0: off
1: on
2: on only if someone appears to have interacted with a flag.
scr_scoreboard_showflags.name: scr_scoreboard_showflags

scr_scoreboard_showfrags.description: Display kills+deaths+teamkills, as determined by fragfile.dat-based conprint parsing. These may be inaccurate if you join mid-game.
scr_scoreboard_showfrags.name: scr_scoreboard_showfrags

scr_scoreboard_showhealth.description:
Display health information when playing mvd/qtv streams.
0: off
1: on
2: show armour too. 3: combined health ('+' says more armour than health allows).
scr_scoreboard_showhealth.name: scr_scoreboard_showhealth

scr_scoreboard_showlocation.description: Display player location names when playing mvd/qtv streams, if available.
scr_scoreboard_showlocation.name: scr_scoreboard_showlocation

scr_scoreboard_showweapon.description: Display weapon information when playing mvd/qtv streams.
scr_scoreboard_showweapon.name: scr_scoreboard_showweapon

scr_scoreboard_teamsort.description: On the scoreboard, sort players by their team BEFORE their personal score.
scr_scoreboard_teamsort.name: scr_scoreboard_teamsort

scr_sshot_compression.description: Requsted compression ratio as a percentage. For jpeg this is the quantisation quality and has a direct impact on image quality vs size. For png this ranges between 0 for best and 100 for worst with final image quality being unchanged because png is loseless.
scr_sshot_compression.name: scr_sshot_compression

scr_sshot_type.description: This specifies the default extension(and thus file format) for screenshots.\nKnown extensions are: png, jpg/jpeg, bmp, pcx, tga, ktx, dds.
scr_sshot_type.name: scr_sshot_type

scr_usekfont.description: Exists for compat with the quake rerelease, changing the behaviour of QC's sprint/bprint/centerprint builtins.
scr_usekfont.name: scr_usekfont

show_fps.description:
Displays the current framerate on-screen.
0: Off.
1: framerate average over a second.
2: Show a frametimes graph (with additional timing info).
-1: Normalized graph that focuses on the variation ignoring base times.
show_fps.name: show_fps

skyroom.description: Specifies the center position of the skyroom's view. Skyrooms are drawn instead of skyboxes (typically with their own skybox around them). Entities in skyrooms will be drawn only when r_ignoreentpvs is 0. Can also be set with the _skyroom worldspawn key. This is overriden by csqc's VF_SKYROOM_CAMERA.
skyroom.name: skyroom

snd_ignorecueloops.description: Ignores cue commands in wav files, for q3 compat.
snd_ignorecueloops.name: snd_ignorecueloops

snd_ignoregamespeed.description: When set, allows sounds to desynchronise with game time or demo speeds.
snd_ignoregamespeed.name: snd_ignoregamespeed

snd_loadasstereo.description: Force mono sounds to load as if stereo ones, to waste memory. Not normally useful.
snd_loadasstereo.name: snd_loadasstereo

snd_playbackrate.description: Debugging cvar that changes the playback rate of all new sounds.
snd_playbackrate.name: snd_playbackrate

sv_aim.description: The value should be cos(angle), where angle is the greatest allowed angle from which to deviate from the direction the shot would have been along. Values >1 thus disable auto-aim. This can be overridden with setinfo aim 0.73.
sv_aim.name: sv_aim

sv_antilag.description:
Attempt to backdate impacts to compensate for lag via the MOVE_ANTILAG feature.
0=completely off.
1=mod-controlled (default).
2=forced, which might break certain uses of traceline.
3=Also attempt to recalculate trace start positions to avoid lagged knockbacks.
sv_antilag.name: sv_antilag

sv_autooffload.description: Automatically start the server in a separate process, so that sporadic or persistent gamecode slowdowns do not affect visual framerates (equivelent to the mapcluster command). Note: Offloaded servers have separate cvar+command states which may complicate usage.
sv_autooffload.name: sv_autooffload

sv_autosave.description: Interval for autosaves, in minutes. Set to 0 to disable autosave.
sv_autosave.name: sv_autosave

sv_banproxies.description: If enabled, anyone connecting via known proxy software will be refused entry. This should aid with blocking aimbots, but is only reliable for certain public proxies.
sv_banproxies.name: sv_banproxies

sv_bigcoords.description:
Uses floats for coordinates instead of 16bit values.
Also boosts angle precision, so can be useful even on small maps.
Affects clients thusly:
QW: enforces a mandatory protocol extension
DP: enables DPP7 protocol support
NQ: uses RMQ protocol (protocol 999).
sv_bigcoords.name: sv_bigcoords

sv_brokenmovetypes.description: Emulate vanilla quakeworld by forcing MOVETYPE_WALK on all players. Shouldn't be used for any games other than QuakeWorld.
sv_brokenmovetypes.name: sv_brokenmovetypes

sv_calcphs.description: Enables culling of sound effects. 0=always skip phs. Sounds are globally broadcast. 1=always generate phs. Sounds are always culled. On large maps the phs will be dumped to disk. 2=On large single-player maps, generation of phs is skipped. Otherwise like option 1.
sv_calcphs.name: sv_calcphs

sv_crypt_rcon.description:
Controls whether the rcon password must be hashed or not. Hashed passwords also partially prevent replay attacks, but does NOT prevent malicious actors from reading the commands/results.
0: completely insecure. ONLY allows plain-text passwords. Do not use.
1: Mandatory hashing (recommended).
Empty: Allow either, whether the password is secure or not is purely the client's responsibility/fault. Only use this for comptibility with old clients.
sv_crypt_rcon.name: sv_crypt_rcon

sv_csqcdebug.description: Inject packet size information for data directed to csqc.
sv_csqcdebug.name: sv_csqcdebug

sv_cullentities_trace.description: Attempt to cull non-player entities using tracelines as an extreeme anti-wallhack.
sv_cullentities_trace.name: sv_cullentities_trace

sv_cullplayers_trace.description: Attempt to cull player entities using tracelines as an anti-wallhack.
sv_cullplayers_trace.name: sv_cullplayers_trace

sv_demoAutoCompress.description: Specifies whether to compress demos as they're recorded.\n0 = no compression.\n1 = gzip compression.
sv_demoAutoCompress.name: sv_demoAutoCompress

sv_demoAutoRecord.description: If set, automatically record demos.\n-1: record on client connection only.\n1+: record once there's this many active players on the server (or if connected to a remote server).
sv_demoAutoRecord.name: sv_demoAutoRecord

sv_demoClearOld.description: Automatically delete demos to keep the demos count reasonable.
sv_demoClearOld.name: sv_demoClearOld

sv_demoDirAlt.description: Provides a fallback directory name for demo downloads, for when sv_demoDir doesn't contain the requested demo.
sv_demoDirAlt.name: sv_demoDirAlt

sv_demoExtensions.description:
Enables protocol extensions within MVDs. This will cause older/non-fte clients to error upon playback.
0: off.
1: all extensions.
2: extensions also supported by a certain other engine.
sv_demoExtensions.name: sv_demoExtensions

sv_demoMaxDirAge.description: Maximum allowed age for demos, any older demos will be deleted when sv_demoClearOld is set (this doesn't prevent recording new demos).
sv_demoMaxDirAge.name: sv_demoMaxDirAge

sv_demoMaxDirCount.description: Maximum allowed serverside mvds to record. Set to 0 to remove the limit. New demos cannot be recorded once this many demos have already been recorded.
sv_demoMaxDirCount.name: sv_demoMaxDirCount

sv_demoMaxDirSize.description: Maximum allowed serverside storage space for mvds. set to blank to remove the limit. New demos cannot be recorded once this size is reached.
sv_demoMaxDirSize.name: sv_demoMaxDirSize

sv_demoMaxSize.description: Demos will be truncated to be no larger than this size.
sv_demoMaxSize.name: sv_demoMaxSize

sv_demoPings.description: Interval between ping updates in mvds
sv_demoPings.name: sv_demoPings

sv_demoUseCache.description: If set, demo data will be flushed only periodically
sv_demoUseCache.name: sv_demoUseCache

sv_demo_write_csqc.description: Writes a copy of the csprogs into recorded demos. This ensures that the demo can be played back despite future gamecode changes.
sv_demo_write_csqc.name: sv_demo_write_csqc

sv_dlURL.description: Provides clients with an external url from which they can obtain pk3s/packages from an external http server instead of having to download over udp.
sv_dlURL.name: sv_dlURL

sv_ftp_port_range.description: Specifies the port range for the server to create listening sockets for 'active' ftp connections, to work around NAT/firewall issues.\nMost FTP clients should use passive connections, but there's still some holdouts like windows.
sv_ftp_port_range.name: sv_ftp_port_range

sv_fulllevel.description: User accounts with an access level greater than this may write anywhere, including the gamedir. Note that setting this low is increadibly risky. An empty value will be understood to never give this permission.
sv_fulllevel.name: sv_fulllevel

sv_fullredirect.description: This is the ip:port to redirect players to when the server is full
sv_fullredirect.name: sv_fullredirect

sv_gameplayfix_blowupfallenzombies.description: Allow findradius to find non-solid entities. This may break certain mods. It is better for mods to use FL_FINDABLE_NONSOLID instead.
sv_gameplayfix_blowupfallenzombies.name: sv_gameplayfix_blowupfallenzombies

sv_gameplayfix_droptofloorstartsolid.description: When droptofloor fails, this causes a second attemp, but with traceline instead.
sv_gameplayfix_droptofloorstartsolid.name: sv_gameplayfix_droptofloorstartsolid

sv_gameplayfix_findradiusdistancetobox.description: When 1, findradius checks to the nearest part of the entity instead of only its origin, making it find slightly more entities.
sv_gameplayfix_findradiusdistancetobox.name: sv_gameplayfix_findradiusdistancetobox

sv_gameplayfix_grenadebouncedownslopes.description: MOVETYPE_BOUNCE speeds are calculated relative to the impacted surface, instead of the vertical, reducing the chance of grenades just sitting there on slopes.
sv_gameplayfix_grenadebouncedownslopes.name: sv_gameplayfix_grenadebouncedownslopes

sv_gameplayfix_multiplethinks.description: Enables multiple thinks per entity per frame so small nextthink times are accurate. QuakeWorld mods expect a value of 1, while NQ expects 0.
sv_gameplayfix_multiplethinks.name: sv_gameplayfix_multiplethinks

sv_gameplayfix_nolinknonsolid.description: When 0, setorigin et al will not link the entity into the collision nodes (which is faster, especially if you have a lot of non-solid entities. When 1, allows entities to freely switch between .solid values (except for SOLID_BSP) without relinking. A lot of DP mods assume a value of 1 and will bug out otherwise, while 0 will restore a bugs present in various mods.
sv_gameplayfix_nolinknonsolid.name: sv_gameplayfix_nolinknonsolid

sv_gameplayfix_setmodelrealbox.description: Vanilla setmodel will setsize the entity to a hardcoded size for non-bsp models. This cvar will always use the real size of the model instead, but will require that the server actually loads the model.
sv_gameplayfix_setmodelrealbox.name: sv_gameplayfix_setmodelrealbox

sv_gameplayfix_setmodelsize_qw.description: The setmodel builtin will act as a setsize for QuakeWorld mods also.
sv_gameplayfix_setmodelsize_qw.name: sv_gameplayfix_setmodelsize_qw

sv_gameplayfix_spawnbeforethinks.description: Fixes an issue where player thinks (including Pre+Post) can be called before PutClientInServer. Unfortunately at least one mod depends upon PreThink being called first in order to correctly determine spawn positions.
sv_gameplayfix_spawnbeforethinks.name: sv_gameplayfix_spawnbeforethinks

sv_gameplayfix_stepdown.description: Attempt to step down steps, instead of only up them. Affects non-predicted movetype_walk.
sv_gameplayfix_stepdown.name: sv_gameplayfix_stepdown

sv_gameplayfix_trappedwithin.description: Blocks further entity movement when an entity is already inside another entity. This ensures that bsp precision issues cannot allow the entity to completely pass through eg the world.
sv_gameplayfix_trappedwithin.name: sv_gameplayfix_trappedwithin

sv_getrealip.description:
Attempt to obtain a more reliable IP for clients, rather than just their proxy.
0: Don't attempt.
1: Unreliable checks.
2: Validate if possible.
3: Mandatory validation.
sv_getrealip.name: sv_getrealip

sv_guidkey.description: If set, clients will calculate their GUID values against this string instead of the server's IP address. This allows consistency between multiple servers (for stats tracking), but do NOT treat the client's GUID as something that is secure.
sv_guidkey.name: sv_guidkey

sv_heartbeat_checks.description: Report when sv_public 1 fails due to PROBABLE router/NAT issues.
sv_heartbeat_checks.name: sv_heartbeat_checks

sv_heartbeat_interval.description: Interval between heartbeats. Low values are abusive, high values may cause NAT/ghost issues.
sv_heartbeat_interval.name: sv_heartbeat_interval

sv_limittics.description: The maximum number of ticks that may be run within a frame, to allow the server to catch up if it stalled or if sv_maxtic is too low.
sv_limittics.name: sv_limittics

sv_listen_dp.description: Allows the server to respond with the DP-specific handshake protocol.\nWarning: this can potentially get confused with quake2, and results in race conditions with both vanilla netquake and quakeworld protocols.\nOn the plus side, DP clients can usually be identified correctly, enabling a model+sound limit boost.
sv_listen_dp.name: sv_listen_dp

sv_listen_nq.description:
Allow new (net)quake clients to connect to the server.
0 = don't let them in.
1 = allow them in (WARNING: this allows 'qsmurf' DOS attacks).
2 = accept (net)quake clients by emulating a challenge (as secure as QW/Q2 but does not fully conform to the NQ protocol).
You may also need to set net_enable_dtls if you wish for the rerelease's client to connect.
sv_listen_nq.name: sv_listen_nq

sv_listen_qw.description: Specifies whether normal clients are allowed to connect.
sv_listen_qw.name: sv_listen_qw

sv_maxaim.description: The maximum acceptable angle for autoaiming.
sv_maxaim.name: sv_maxaim

sv_maxdrate.description: This cvar controls the maximum number of bytes sent to each player per second while that player is downloading.\nIf this cvar is set to 0, there will be NO CAP for download rates (if the user's drate is empty/0 too, then expect really fast+abusive downloads that could potentially be considered denial of service attacks)
sv_maxdrate.name: sv_maxdrate

sv_maxrate.description: This controls the maximum number of bytes any indivual player may receive (when not downloading). The individual user's rate will also be controlled by the user's rate cvar.
sv_maxrate.name: sv_maxrate

sv_maxtic.description: The maximum interval between running physics frames. If the value is too low, multiple physics interations might be run at a time (based upon sv_limittics). Set to 0 for fixed-interval ticks, which may be required if ODE is used.
sv_maxtic.name: sv_maxtic

sv_minping.description: Simulate fake lag for any players with a ping under the value specified here. Value is in milliseconds.
sv_minping.name: sv_minping

sv_mintic.description: The minimum interval between running physics frames.
sv_mintic.name: sv_mintic

sv_nailhack.description: If set to 1, disables the nail entity networking optimisation. This hack was popularised by qizmo which recommends it for better compression. Also allows clients to interplate nail positions and add trails.
sv_nailhack.name: sv_nailhack

sv_nopvs.description: Set to 1 to ignore pvs on the server. This can make wallhacks more dangerous, so should only be used for debugging.
sv_nopvs.name: sv_nopvs

sv_nqplayerphysics.description: Disable player prediction and run NQ-style player physics instead. This can be used for compatibility with mods that expect exact behaviour. A value of 2 will not block prediction, and may be juddery/jerky/swimmy.
sv_nqplayerphysics.name: sv_nqplayerphysics

sv_phs.description: If 1, do not use the phs. It is generally better to use sv_calcphs instead, and leave this as 1.
sv_phs.name: sv_phs

sv_ping_ignorepl.description: If 1, ping times reported for players will ignore the effects of packetloss on ping times. 0 is slightly more honest, but less useful for connection diagnosis.
sv_ping_ignorepl.name: sv_ping_ignorepl

sv_playerslots.description: Specify maximum number of player/spectator/bot slots, new value takes effect on the next map (this may result in players getting kicked). This should generally be set to maxclients+maxspectators. Leave blank for a default value.\nMaximum value of . Values above 16 will result in issues with vanilla NQ clients. Effective values other than 32 will result in issues with vanilla QW clients.
sv_playerslots.name: sv_playerslots

sv_port.description: Port number to list on for inbound udp-based connections (including dtls variants). Can be a list for multiple ports. If ips are included then binds to that specific interface. Whether any specific protocol is accepted depends upon other settings.
sv_port.name: sv_port

sv_port_ipv6.description: Port to use for incoming ipv6 udp connections. Due to hybrid sockets this might not be needed. You can specify an ipv4 address:port for a second ipv4 port if you want.
sv_port_ipv6.name: sv_port_ipv6

sv_port_natpmp.description: If set (typically to 5351), automatically configures your router's port forwarding. You can instead specify the full ip address of your router (192.168.1.1:5351 for example). Your router must have NAT-PMP supported and enabled.
sv_port_natpmp.name: sv_port_natpmp

sv_port_rtc.description: This specifies the broker url to use to obtain clients from. If the hostname is ommitted, it'll come from the manifest. If omitted, the broker service will randomize the resource part, so be sure to tell your friends the path reported by eg status rather than just this cvar value. Or just set it to 'rtc:///example' and tell clients to connect to the same sservevalue.
sv_port_rtc.name: sv_port_rtc

sv_port_tcp.description: Port number to list on for inbound tcp-based connections (including tls variants). Can be a list for multiple ports. If ips are included then binds to that specific interface. Whether any specific protocol is accepted depends upon other settings.
sv_port_tcp.name: sv_port_tcp

sv_port_tcp6.description: Equivelent to sv_port_tcp, but port numbers are assumed to be ipv6 only. relevant only when not using hybrid sockets.
sv_port_tcp6.name: sv_port_tcp6

sv_progs.description: Specifies the filename of the gamecode to use serverside. Empty means autodetect - typically loading either progs or qwprogs depending on gamedir priority, then based upon deathmatch settings.
sv_progs.name: sv_progs

sv_protocol.description: Specifies which protocol extensions to force. Clients which do not support the named protocols will be kicked. Recognised values: fte1 fte2 csqc.
sv_protocol.name: sv_protocol

sv_protocol_nq.description:
Specifies the default protocol to use for new NQ clients. This is only relevent for clients that do not report their supported protocols. Supported values are
0 = autodetect
15 = vanilla
666 = fitzquake
999 = rmq protocol
The sv_bigcoords cvar forces upgrades as required.
sv_protocol_nq.name: sv_protocol_nq

sv_public.description:
-1: Fully blocks all inbound connections.
0: Disable subscribing to master servers (for private lan-only games).
1: Subscribe to public master servers. Your IP address will be listed publicly. Make sure your Router/NAT+Firewall are set to allow inbound connections.
2: Subscribe to a broker master, allowing firewall hole punching.
sv_public.name: sv_public

sv_pupglow.description: Instructs clients to enable hexen2-style powerup pulsing.
sv_pupglow.name: sv_pupglow

sv_pure.description:
The most evil cvar in the world, many clients will ignore this.
0=standard quake rules.
1=clients should prefer files within packages present on the server.
2=clients should use *only* files within packages present on the server.
Due to quake 1.01/1.06 differences, a setting of 2 only works in total conversions.
sv_pure.name: sv_pure

sv_realip_kick.description: Kicks clients if their realip could not be validated to the level specified by sv_getrealip.
sv_realip_kick.name: sv_realip_kick

sv_realiphostname_ipv4.description: This is the server's public ip:port. This is needed for realip to work when the autodetected/local ip is not globally routable
sv_realiphostname_ipv4.name: sv_realiphostname_ipv4

sv_realiphostname_ipv6.description: This is the server's public ip:port. This is needed for realip to work when the autodetected/local ip is not globally routable
sv_realiphostname_ipv6.name: sv_realiphostname_ipv6

sv_reconnectlimit.description: Blocks dupe connection within the specified length of time .
sv_reconnectlimit.name: sv_reconnectlimit

sv_reliable_sound.description: Causes all sounds to be sent reliably, so they will not be missed due to packetloss. However, this will cause them to be delayed somewhat, and slightly bursty. This can be overriden using the 'rsnd' userinfo setting (either forced on or forced off). Note: this does not affect sounds attached to particle effects.
sv_reliable_sound.name: sv_reliable_sound

sv_reportheartbeats.description: Print a notice each time a heartbeat is sent to a master server. When set to 2, the message will be displayed once.
sv_reportheartbeats.name: sv_reportheartbeats

sv_savefmt.description:
Specifies the format used for the saved game.
0=legacy.
1=fte
2=binary
sv_savefmt.name: sv_savefmt

sv_serverip.description: Set this cvar to the server's public ip address if the server is behind a firewall and cannot detect its own public address. Providing a port is required if the firewall/nat remaps it, but is otherwise optional.
sv_serverip.name: sv_serverip

sv_showconnectionlessmessages.description: Display a line describing each connectionless message that arrives on the server. Primarily a debugging feature, but also potentially useful to admins.
sv_showconnectionlessmessages.name: sv_showconnectionlessmessages

sv_showpredloss.description: Print messages whenever input frames are ignored or forced serverside, to prevent speedcheats or hover cheats. Any such prints will be accompanied by prediction misses in the named client.
sv_showpredloss.name: sv_showpredloss

sv_specprint.description:
Bitfield that controls which player events spectators see when tracking that player.
&1: spectators will see centerprints.
&2: spectators will see sprints (pickup messages etc).
&4: spectators will receive console commands, this is potentially risky.
Individual spectators can use 'setinfo sp foo' to limit this setting.
sv_specprint.name: sv_specprint

sv_timestamplen.description: Limits clock skew to reduce (delayed) replay attacks
sv_timestamplen.name: sv_timestamplen

sv_use_dns.description: Performs a reverse-dns lookup in order to report more info about where clients are connecting from.
sv_use_dns.name: sv_use_dns

sv_userinfo_bytelimit.description: This is the maximum number of bytes that may be stored into each user's userinfo. Note that this includes key names too.
sv_userinfo_bytelimit.name: sv_userinfo_bytelimit

sv_userinfo_keylimit.description: This is the maximum number of userinfo keys each user may create.
sv_userinfo_keylimit.name: sv_userinfo_keylimit

sv_voip_echo.description: Echo voice packets back to their sender, a debug/test setting.
sv_voip_echo.name: sv_voip_echo

sv_voip_record.description: Record voicechat into mvds. Requires player support. 0=noone, 1=everyone, 2=spectators only
sv_voip_record.name: sv_voip_record

sv_wallfriction.description: Additional friction when running into walls
sv_wallfriction.name: sv_wallfriction

sv_writelevel.description: Specifies the required trust level at which user accounts may write to the user-specific subdir of /uploads/USERNAME/*. If blank, then no uploads are permitted
sv_writelevel.name: sv_writelevel

sys_clockprecision.description: Attempts to control windows' interrupt interval, in milliseconds. This can cause windows to give better clock precision and shorter waits, but also more overhead from process rescheduling.
sys_clockprecision.name: sys_clockprecision

sys_clocktype.description:
Controls which system clock to base timings from.
0: auto
1: gettimeofday (may be discontinuous).
2: monotonic.
sys_clocktype.name: sys_clocktype

sys_colorconsole.description: Parse colour escapes, with ansi colours on stdout.
sys_colorconsole.name: sys_colorconsole

sys_keepscreenon.description: If set, the screen will never darken. This might cost some extra battery power, but then so will running a 3d engine.
sys_keepscreenon.name: sys_keepscreenon

sys_orientation.description: Specifies what angle to render quake at.\nValid values are: sensor (autodetect), landscape, portrait, reverselandscape, reverseportrait
sys_orientation.name: sys_orientation

timeout.description: Connections will time out if no packets are received for this duration of time.
timeout.name: timeout

tls_ignorecertificateerrors.description: This should NEVER be set to 1!
tls_ignorecertificateerrors.name: tls_ignorecertificateerrors

tls_provider.description: Controls which TLS provider to use.
tls_provider.name: tls_provider

tts_mode.description:
Text to speech
0: off
1: Read only chat messages with a leading 'tts ' prefix.
2: Read all chat messages
3: Read every single console print.
tts_mode.name: tts_mode

utf8_enable.description: When 1, changes the qc builtins to act upon codepoints instead of bytes. Do not use unless com_parseutf8 is also set.
utf8_enable.name: utf8_enable

v_bonusflash.description: Controls the strength of temporary screen flashes when picking up items (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_bonusflash.name: v_bonusflash

v_contentblend.description: Controls the strength of underwater colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_contentblend.name: v_contentblend

v_cshift_empty.description: The colour tint to use when in the open air (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.
v_cshift_empty.name: v_cshift_empty

v_cshift_lava.description: The colour tint to use when burried in lava (ouchie!) (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.
v_cshift_lava.name: v_cshift_lava

v_cshift_slime.description: The colour tint to use when submerged in slime (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.
v_cshift_slime.name: v_cshift_slime

v_cshift_water.description: The colour tint to use when underwater (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.
v_cshift_water.name: v_cshift_water

v_damagecshift.description: Controls the strength of damage-taken colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_damagecshift.name: v_damagecshift

v_deathtilt.description: Specifies whether to tilt the view when dead.
v_deathtilt.name: v_deathtilt

v_depthsortentities.description: Reorder entities for transparency such that the furthest entities are drawn first, allowing nearer transparent entities to draw over the top of them.
v_depthsortentities.name: v_depthsortentities

v_gammainverted.description: Boolean that controls whether the gamma should be inverted (like quake) or not.
v_gammainverted.name: v_gammainverted

v_gunkick.description: Controls the strength of view angle changes when firing weapons.
v_gunkick.name: v_gunkick

v_gunkick_q2.description: Controls the strength of view angle changes when firing weapons (in Quake2).
v_gunkick_q2.name: v_gunkick_q2

v_idlescale.description: Enable swishing of the view (whether idle or otherwise). Often used for concussion effects.
v_idlescale.name: v_idlescale

v_kickpitch.description: This controls part of the strength of viewangle changes from taking damage.
v_kickpitch.name: v_kickpitch

v_kickroll.description: This controls part of the strength of viewangle changes from taking damage.
v_kickroll.name: v_kickroll

v_kicktime.description: This controls how long viewangle changes from taking damage will last.
v_kicktime.name: v_kicktime

v_pentcshift.description: Controls the strength of pentagram-of-protection colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_pentcshift.name: v_pentcshift

v_quadcshift.description: Controls the strength of quad-damage colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_quadcshift.name: v_quadcshift

v_ringcshift.description: Controls the strength of ring-of-invisibility colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_ringcshift.name: v_ringcshift

v_suitcshift.description: Controls the strength of envirosuit colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).
v_suitcshift.name: v_suitcshift

vid_baseheight.description: Specifies a mod's target height and used only when the 2d scale is not otherwise forced. Unlike vid_conheight the size is not fixed and will be padded to avoid inconsistent filtering.
vid_baseheight.name: vid_baseheight

vid_bpp.description: The number of colour bits to request from the renedering context
vid_bpp.name: vid_bpp

vid_conautoscale.description: Changes the 2d scale, including hud, console, and fonts. To specify an explicit font size, divide the desired 'point' size by 8 to get the scale. High values will be clamped to maintain at least a 320*200 virtual size.
vid_conautoscale.name: vid_conautoscale

vid_conheight.description: Specifies the virtual height of the screen. If 0, will be inferred by vid_conwidth or other settings, according to aspect etc.
vid_conheight.name: vid_conheight

vid_conwidth.description: Specifies the virtual width of the screen. Should generally be left as 0 to allow the correct aspect to be used despite video mode changes.
vid_conwidth.name: vid_conwidth

vid_depthbits.description: The number of depth bits to request from the renedering context. Try 24.
vid_depthbits.name: vid_depthbits

vid_desktopgamma.description: Apply gamma ramps upon the desktop rather than the window.
vid_desktopgamma.name: vid_desktopgamma

vid_desktopsettings.description: Ignore the values of vid_width and vid_height, and just use the same settings that are used for the desktop.
vid_desktopsettings.name: vid_desktopsettings

vid_devicename.description: Specifies which video device to try to use. If blank or invalid then one will be guessed.
vid_devicename.name: vid_devicename

vid_dpi_x.description: For mods that need to determine the physical screen size (like with touchscreens). 0 means unknown
vid_dpi_x.name: vid_dpi_x

vid_dpi_y.description: For mods that need to determine the physical screen size (like with touchscreens). 0 means unknown
vid_dpi_y.name: vid_dpi_y

vid_fullscreen.description:
Specifies whether the game should be fullscreen or not (requires vid_restart).
0: Run in a resizable window, which can be manually maximized (with borders).
1: Traditional fullscreen-exclusive video mode with mode switching and everything.
2: Simply maximize the window and hide any borders without interfering with any other parts of the system.
vid_fullscreen.name: vid_fullscreen

vid_gl_context_compatibility.description: Requests an OpenGL context with fixed-function backwards compat.
vid_gl_context_compatibility.name: vid_gl_context_compatibility

vid_gl_context_debug.description: Requests a debug opengl context. This provides better error oreporting.
vid_gl_context_debug.name: vid_gl_context_debug

vid_gl_context_es.description: Requests an OpenGLES context. Be sure to set vid_gl_context_version to 2 or so.
vid_gl_context_es.name: vid_gl_context_es

vid_gl_context_forwardcompatible.description: Requests an opengl context with no depricated features enabled.
vid_gl_context_forwardcompatible.name: vid_gl_context_forwardcompatible

vid_gl_context_noerror.description: Disables OpenGL's error checks for a small performance speedup. May cause segfaults if stuff wasn't properly implemented/tested.
vid_gl_context_noerror.name: vid_gl_context_noerror

vid_gl_context_robustness.description: Attempt to enforce extra buffer protection in the gl driver, but can be slower with pre-gl3 hardware.
vid_gl_context_robustness.name: vid_gl_context_robustness

vid_gl_context_selfreset.description: Upon hardware failure, have the engine create a new context instead of depending on the drivers to restore everything. This can help to avoid graphics drivers randomly killing your game, and can help reduce memory requirements.
vid_gl_context_selfreset.name: vid_gl_context_selfreset

vid_gl_context_version.description: Specifies the version of OpenGL to try to create.
vid_gl_context_version.name: vid_gl_context_version

vid_hardwaregamma.description: Use hardware gamma ramps. 0=ugly texture-based gamma, 1=glsl(windowed) or hardware(fullscreen), 2=always glsl, 3=always hardware gamma (disabled if hardware doesn't support), 4=scene-only gamma.
vid_hardwaregamma.name: vid_hardwaregamma

vid_height.description: The screen height to attempt to use, in physical pixels. 0 means use desktop resolution.
vid_height.name: vid_height

vid_minsize.description: Specifies a mod's minimum virtual size (to be set inside the mod's default.cfg file). The virtual size will always be at least this big. Windows may not be resized below this value either (which may reduce video mode options), but might require a vid_restart to take effect when switching between mods.
vid_minsize.name: vid_minsize

vid_multisample.description: The number of samples to use for Multisample AntiAliasing (aka: msaa). A value of 1 explicitly disables it.
vid_multisample.name: vid_multisample

vid_preservegamma.description: Restore initial hardware gamma ramps when quitting.
vid_preservegamma.name: vid_preservegamma

vid_renderer.description: Specifies which backend is used. Values that might work are: sv (dedicated server), headless (null renderer), vk (vulkan), gl (opengl), egl (opengl es), d3d9 (direct3d 9), d3d11 (direct3d 11, with default hardware rendering), d3d11 warp (direct3d 11, with software rendering).
vid_renderer.name: vid_renderer

vid_srgb.description:
-1: Only the framebuffer should use sRGB colourspace, textures and colours will be assumed to be linear. This has the effect of just brightening the screen according to a gamma ramp of about 2.2 (or .45 in quake's backwards gamma terms).
0: Off. Colour blending will be wrong, you're likely to see obvious banding.
1: Use sRGB extensions/support to ensure that the lighting aproximately matches real-world lighting (required for PBR).
2: Attempt to use a linear floating-point framebuffer, which should enable monitor support for HDR.
Note that driver behaviour varies by a disturbing amount, and much of the documentation conflicts with itself (the term 'linear' is awkward when the eye's perception of linear is non-linear).
vid_srgb.name: vid_srgb

vid_triplebuffer.description: Specifies whether the hardware is forcing tripplebuffering on us, this is the number of extra page swaps required before old data has been completely overwritten.
vid_triplebuffer.name: vid_triplebuffer

vid_width.description: The screen width to attempt to use, in physical pixels. 0 means use desktop resolution.
vid_width.name: vid_width

vid_winthread.description: When enabled, window messages will be handled by a separate thread. This allows the game to continue rendering when Microsoft Windows blocks while resizing, etc.
vid_winthread.name: vid_winthread

vid_wndalpha.description: When running windowed, specifies the window's transparency level.
vid_wndalpha.name: vid_wndalpha

vk_amd_rasterization_order.description: Enables the use of relaxed rasterization ordering, for a small speedup at the minor risk of a little zfighting.
vk_amd_rasterization_order.name: vk_amd_rasterization_order

vk_busywait.description: Force busy waiting until the GPU finishes doing its thing.
vk_busywait.name: vk_busywait

vk_debug.description: Register a debug handler to display driver/layer messages. 2 enables the standard validation layers.
vk_debug.name: vk_debug

vk_dualqueue.description: Attempt to use a separate queue for presentation. Blank for default.
vk_dualqueue.name: vk_dualqueue

vk_khr_dedicated_allocation.description: Flag vulkan memory allocations as dedicated, where applicable.
vk_khr_dedicated_allocation.name: vk_khr_dedicated_allocation

vk_stagingbuffers.description: Configures which dynamic buffers are copied into gpu memory for rendering, instead of reading from shared memory. Empty for default settings.\nAccepted chars are u(niform), e(lements), v(ertex), 0(none).
vk_stagingbuffers.name: vk_stagingbuffers

vk_submissionthread.description: Execute submits+presents on a thread dedicated to executing them. This may be a significant speedup on certain drivers.
vk_submissionthread.name: vk_submissionthread

vk_usememorypools.description: Allocates memory pools for sub allocations. Vulkan has a limit to the number of memory allocations allowed so this should always be enabled, however at this time FTE is unable to reclaim pool memory, and would require periodic vid_restarts to flush them.
vk_usememorypools.name: vk_usememorypools

vk_waitfence.description: Waits on fences, instead of semaphores. This is more likely to result in gpu stalls while the cpu waits.
vk_waitfence.name: vk_waitfence

volume.description: Volume level for game sounds (does not affect music, voice, or cinematics).
volume.name: volume

votelevel.description: This is the restriction level of commands that players may vote for. You can reconfigure commands, cvars, or aliases individually. Additionally, aliases can be configured via aliaslevel to be executed at a different level from their restriction level. This can be used to indirectly allow voting for 'map dm4' for instance, without allowing people to vote for every map.
votelevel.name: votelevel

voteminimum.description: At least this many players must vote the same way for the vote to pass.
voteminimum.name: voteminimum

votepercent.description: At least this percentage of players must vote the same way for the vote to pass.
votepercent.name: votepercent

votetime.description: Votes will be discarded after this many minutes
votetime.name: votetime

wasapi_exclusive.description: When set, attempts to take exclusive control of the output device, to the detriment of other programs (causing errors or even crashes in them).\nExclusive mode leaves the game free to change the hardware's playback details, instead of being required to use a single system-wide 'mixer' rate.\nIt should also reduce latency a little.
wasapi_exclusive.name: wasapi_exclusive

wasapi_forcechannels.description: Attempts to force snd_numchannels instead of using the system's default channel count.\nFor this to work, you will need to set wasapi_exclusive 1
wasapi_forcechannels.name: wasapi_forcechannels

wasapi_forcerate.description: Attempts to force snd_khz instead of using the system's default channel count.\nFor this to work, you will need to set wasapi_exclusive 1
wasapi_forcerate.name: wasapi_forcerate

worker_count.description: Specifies the number of worker threads to utilise.
worker_count.name: worker_count

worker_flush.description: If set, process the entire load queue, loading stuff faster but at the risk of stalling the main thread.
worker_flush.name: worker_flush

worker_sleeptime.description: Causes workers to sleep for a period of time after each job.
worker_sleeptime.name: worker_sleeptime

zombietime.description: Client slots will not be reused for this number of seconds.
zombietime.name: zombietime
